Sindiket penyelewengan diesel terbongkar, lori sama ditahan lagi

Iskandar Puteri: Sebuah lori yang sebelum ini dikenakan tindakan kerana terbabit dalam penyelewengan diesel, ditahan lagi di tapak pembinaan di Mukim Pulai, di sini semalam, bersama kira-kira 2,500 liter diesel bersubsidi. Kementerian Perdagangan Dalam Negeri dan Kos Sara Hidup (KPDN) Johor menyita lori berkenaan dalam satu operasi pada jam 7 malam semalam, susulan operasi risikan selama sebulan. Pengarah KPDN Johor, Lilis Saslinda Pornomo berkata, pegawai penguat kuasa menemui lori yang diubah suai dilengkapi tangki simpanan dan peralatan lain, selain diesel bersubsidi. "Hasil pemeriksaan mendapati, lori itu sebelum ini sudah dikenakan tindakan penguatkuasaan membabitkan kesalahan sama. "Dalam operasi ini, lori sama sekali lagi ditemui di premis itu bersama peralatan penyimpanan dan diesel terbabit," katanya dalam satu kenyataan hari ini. Turut disita, dua tangki menyimpan dan mengangkut cecair, sebuah tangki simpanan mudah alih, pam motor elektrik, meter aliran, hos dan pam bermotor arus terus (DC) dipercayai digunakan untuk memindahkan diesel bersubsidi berkenaan. Dua lelaki dipercayai pekerja di tapak berkenaan turut ditahan bagi membantu siasatan. Jumlah keseluruhan nilai barangan yang disita dianggarkan RM33,075. Lilis berkata, kes itu disiasat mengikut Seksyen 20(1) Akta Kawalan Bekalan 1961 kerana disyaki menyimpan atau memindahkan barang kawalan di premis yang tidak dilesenkan atau diberi kebenaran oleh Pengawal Bekalan.

Seremban: Ketua jurulatih Negeri Sembilan FC (NSFC), Daniel Gimenez Alcaniz mengakui keliru dengan situasi yang berlaku terhadap pasukan bimbingannya selepas tewas kepada Kelantan City FC dengan agregat 3-4, sekali gus tersingkir dalam saingan Piala FA, musim ini. Meskipun mencatat kemenangan 3-2, dalam aksi timbal balik di Stadium Tuanku Abdul Rahman, Paroi, petang semalam, namun ia tidak cukup untuk skuad Hobin Jang Hobin melayakkan diri ke peringkat suku akhir saingan kalah mati itu selepas mereka tewas 0-2 kepada Kelantan City di Kota Bharu, sebelum ini. Alcaniz berkata, beliau cuba untuk memahami hakikat sebenar terhadap apa yang pemain persembahkan dalam perlawanan semalam ketika segala persiapan terbaik sudah cuba dilakukan termasuk perancangan taktikal bagi menghadapi saingan penentuan itu. "Secara jujurnya, saya cuba untuk memahami mereka (pemain) dan perlawanan ini (semalam). Adakah pemain tidak bersedia 100 peratus atau tidak memahami (tugasan) atau tidak cukup sihat dan perlukan masa untuk lebih bersedia. "Saya tak tahu nak cakap apa dan tak tahu nak salahkan siapa dengan apa yang berlaku tadi apabila penjaga gol keluar jauh dari kawasan gol, yang sekali gus memberi peluang pemain lawan menjaringkan gol," kata Alcaniz kepada media selepas perlawanan. Pengendali berpengalaman dari Sepanyol itu jelas kecewa dengan corak persembahan anak buahnya kerana ia tidak seperti apa yang beliau rancangkan sebelum perlawanan. "Saya faham kita sudah kalah (pada aksi pertama) tapi saya tak faham apa yang berlaku pada separuh masa tadi (kesilapan demi kesilapan), ia tidak sepatutnya berlaku," katanya. Alcaniz berkata, pemain Negeri Sembilan juga kerap kehilangan bola sekali gus memudahkan pemain lawan mengambil kesempatan untuk mengawal permainan dan kemudian melakukan serangan pantas ke kawasan gol. "Apabila pemain kerap kehilangan bola, ia memberi kesan kepada keseluruhan jentera pasukan. Apa yang saya boleh cakapkan ialah pemain dan penjaga gol perlu kekal di posisi dan lindungi kawasan sendiri dari pihak lawan. "Ini apa yang saya berikan semasa latihan selama ini, tetapi ia seperti tidak menjadi," tegas pengendali berusia 42 tahun itu. Beliau berharap pasukannya mendapat peluang yang lebih baik selepas ini kerana apa yang telah berlaku tidak boleh patah balik dan pemain terpaksa menerima hakikat bahawa cabaran pasukan dalam saingan Piala FA musim ini sudah terhenti. "Kalau kita kalah, kita kalah satu pasukan dan begitu sebaliknya. Saya berharap ada lagi peluang buat pasukan untuk bangkit dengan persembahan lebih baik selepas ini. "Kami perlu bersatu dan kuat semula untuk cabaran liga yang masih panjang. Kami perlu lebih bersedia selepas ini kerana akan menghadapi Johor Datul Ta`zim (JDT) dan berharap mampu peroleh keputusan yang baik dalam liga," katanya. Pada aksi semalam, Negeri Sembilan terlebih dahulu berada di depan menerusi jaringan Yusuke Minagawa pada minit kelima disusuli sepakan penalti oleh Akhyar Rashid (minit ke-36). Kelantan City kemudian menyamakan kedudukan hasil jaringan Dandy Abdullah (minit ke-52) dan Muhammad Asraff Alifuddin Yasin (minit ke-55) manakala gol ketiga Negeri Sembilan dijaringkan oleh Park Yiyoung pada minit ke-89.

Azeez Rahim, 2 bekas pegawai TH direman dua hari

KUALA LUMPUR: Bekas Pengerusi Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim direman dua hari bermula hari ini. Perintah reman itu dikeluarkan oleh Penolong Kanan Pendaftar, Mohamad Afiq Zuber selepas permohonan oleh pihak polis bagi membantu siasatan kes tipu berkait pemberian hibah TH. Difahamkan, Abdul Azeez turut ditahan reman bersama dua lagi individu iaitu bekas Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif TH dan bekas Ketua Pegawai Kewangan TH. Peguam, Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad mewakili ketiga-tiga itu berkata, perintah reman itu dikeluarkan mengikut Seksyen 420 Kanun Keseksaan. “Kita berhujah mengatakan tidak perlu ada tahanan reman lanjut kerana laporan RCI yang jadikan sebagai asas telah pun dilengkapkan. “Sebelum ini, kertas siasatan juga telah diberikan kepada Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC), jadi tiada keperluan. Beliau juga sentiasa memberi kerjasama,” katanya ketika ditemui pemberita selepas prosiding reman. Terdahulu, bekas Ahli Parlimen Baling itu dibawa untuk prosiding reman sebelum menghadapi pertuduhan rasuah di bawah Akta Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM). Sebelum ini, Abdul Azeez direman SPRM selama tujuh hari bermula 26 Ogos lalu bagi membantu siasatan susulan isu dibangkitkan dalam Laporan Suruhanjaya Siasatan Diraja (RCI) TH. Laporan RCI berkaitan TH yang didedahkan kepada umum pada 29 Julai lalu memperincikan kelemahan dalam pengurusan dan operasi dana haji berkenaan bagi tempoh antara 2014 hingga 2020. – UTUSAN
Nahas helikopter KKM: Bapa saudara bantu cari berus gigi, sikat untuk sampel DNA Dr. Ainul

Mohd. Sapri Salleh, 65, berkata, abangnya, Kamarudin, 69, yang merupakan bapa Ainul Baraah menerima panggilan telefon daripada pihak berkuasa kira-kira pukul 10 malam tadi sebelum menerima pesanan agar membawa barangan peribadi anaknya itu ke Sarawak. Katanya, selepas panggilan itu, dia dan abangnya mencari sikat, berus gigi, sarung bantal dan pakaian Ainul Baraah di dalam bilik rumah keluarganya di Kampung Baung di sini. “Ainul Baraah dan suaminya, Muhammad Faiz Abdul Malik, 37, pulang ke kampung selama seminggu ketika cuti sekolah minggu lalu. Jadi, pihak berkuasa meminta keluarga mencari dan membawa barangan peribadi yang ada di rumah sebagai sampel DNA untuk mengesan jenazahnya. “Sekejap sahaja kami berdua mencari kesemua barangan itu kerana ia memang ada di dalam bilik. Kira-kira pukul 10.30 malam tadi, abang dan keluarga terus bergerak ke rumah besannya di Bangi, Selangor sebelum ke Sarawak pagi ini,” katanya ketika dihubungi Kosmo! hari ini. Mohd. Sapri memberitahu, abangnya kelihatan sangat sedih dan letih sebelum bergerak ke Bangi malam tadi. Sementara itu, Kamarudin ketika dihubungi pada pukul 10 pagi tadi berkata, dia ketika ini berada di Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Kuala Lumpur (KLIA), Sepang untuk menaiki pesawat ke Sarawak. “Saya sudah nak naik kapal terbang. Nanti telefon balik,” katanya ringkas. – KOSMO! ONLINE habis

YAKIN perkasa perubatan regeneratif menerusi kerjasama strategik di seluruh negara

KUALA LUMPUR: Yakin Splendour Global Holdings Berhad (YAKIN), peneraju dalam teknologi sel stem mesenchymal tali pusat (UC-MSC) dan penyelesaian bioteknologi termaju, mengumumkan beberapa kerjasama strategik, rancangan untuk memperluaskan fasiliti serta pelantikan duta baharu. Langkah ini merupakan sebahagian daripada usaha YAKIN untuk memperkukuh kedudukan Malaysia sebagai hab serantau bagi perubatan regeneratif, terapi sel dan bioteknologi termaju menerusi anak syarikatnya, Yakin Splendour Sdn Bhd (YSSB). Inisiatif tersebut merangkumi kerjasama dengan penyedia penjagaan kesihatan dan syarikat bioteknologi, peluasan kapasiti pengeluaran sel stem mesenchymal (MSC), pengiktirafan oleh Malaysia Book of Records serta pelantikan legenda badminton negara sebagai duta bagi program perubatan regeneratifnya. Perkembangan ini juga merupakan sebahagian daripada strategi YAKIN untuk memperkukuh keupayaan Malaysia dalam penyelidikan, penghasilan dan aplikasi klinikal sel stem mesenchymal tali pusat (UC-MSC), di samping memperluas kehadirannya di seluruh Lembah Klang, Johor, Perak, Pulau Pinang, Sabah, Sarawak dan negara jiran, Singapura. Datuk Mohammad Yusof Apdal, Timbalan Menteri Sains, Teknologi, dan Inovasi menyaksikan YAKIN menandatangani Memorandum Persefahaman (MoU) bersama rakan strategiknya, sekaligus menandakan satu pencapaian penting dalam perkembangan syarikat. Merkel Clinic Velocity Terima Pengiktirafan Malaysia Book of Records Merkel Clinic Velocity yang beroperasi di bawah Kumpulan YAKIN menerima dua pengiktirafan rasmi daripada Malaysia Book of Records. Klinik itu diiktiraf sebagai penyedia pertama Sel Stem Mesenchymal (MSC) Physoxic di Malaysia dan pembangun pertama sel stem mesenchymal Normoxic Passage 4 (P4). YAKIN berkata, pengiktirafan ini mencerminkan komitmen berterusan dalam pelaburan terhadap penyelidikan dan pembangunan (R&D), bioteknologi termaju serta kerjasama di peringkat antarabangsa, selari dengan usaha Malaysia untuk membangunkan ekosistem perubatan regeneratif dan bioteknologi yang lebih kukuh. Pengarah Yakin Splendour Global Holdings Bhd., Datuk Steven Lai berkata, anugerah tersebut mengiktiraf penyelidikan dan pembangunan yang dilaksanakan syarikat selama bertahun-tahun. “Dua pengiktirafan ini membuktikan hasil usaha penyelidikan dan pembangunan (R&D) yang kami jalankan selama ini, ia dilaksanakan secara teliti selama bertahun-tahun serta mencerminkan komitmen kami terhadap kecemerlangan saintifik. Kami berbangga dapat meletakkan inovasi Malaysia di peta dunia dan membina masa depan di mana terapi sel stem bertaraf dunia dibangunkan, dihasilkan dan disediakan di negara kita sendiri,” kata Datuk Steven Lai. Kerjasama Strategik dengan Hospital UMRA YAKIN secara rasmi memuktamadkan kerjasama strategik dengan Hospital UMRA – sebuah penyedia penjagaan kesihatan swasta multidisiplin terkemuka yang ditubuhkan pada 2006. Kerjasama itu dimeterai secara rasmi menerusi pemeteraian Memorandum Persefahaman (MoU). Perjanjian itu ditandatangani oleh Datuk Steven Lai dan Pengasas serta Pengarah Perubatan Hospital UMRA, Datuk Dr Mohamed Rafi Bin Dato’ Dr Mohammed Feizal. Terletak di Seksyen 13, Shah Alam, Hospital UMRA ialah penyedia penjagaan kesihatan swasta multidisiplin yang ditubuhkan pada 2006 dan memberikan perkhidmatan kepada komuniti pesakit yang majoritinya adalah Muslim. Datuk Steven Lai menjelaskan, kerjasama itu akan menggabungkan kepakaran YAKIN dalam teknologi UC-MSC dengan fokus Hospital UMRA untuk menyediakan penjagaan kesihatan yang mudah diakses dan berkualiti tinggi. “Bersama-sama, kami membawa perubatan regeneratif moden lebih dekat kepada mereka yang memerlukan,” katanya. Kerjasama itu akan mengembangkan kepakaran mendalam YAKIN dalam pengkulturan dan teknologi UC-MSC bersama misi Hospital UMRA untuk menyediakan penjagaan berkualiti tinggi pada harga berpatutan, sejajar dengan aspirasinya untuk menjadi “Hospital Pilihan” bagi komuniti Muslim di seluruh Lembah Klang. Datuk Dr. Mohamed Rafi Bin Dato’ Dr Mohammed Feizal berkata, Hospital UMRA berbesar hati untuk bekerjasama dengan YAKIN bagi menawarkan terapi sel stem bertaraf dunia. “Kerjasama ini memperkukuh misi kami untuk menjadi penyedia penjagaan kesihatan pilihan dengan menyediakan rawatan termaju yang mudah diakses,” katanya. Legenda Adik-Beradik Sidek Dilantik Sebagai Duta Testimoni MSC Physoxic YAKIN melantik legenda sukan negara , Datuk Dr. Hj Mohmed Misbun bin Dato’ Hj Sidek dan Dato’ Seri Hj Mohd. Jalani bin Dato’ Hj Mohd Sidek sebagai Duta Testimoni MSC Physoxic. Pelantikan itu dirasmikan oleh Datuk Steven Lai bersama kedua-dua duta berkenaan. Terkenal dengan kejayaan mereka di Terbuka England serta sebagai anggota penting pasukan Malaysia yang menjuarai Piala Thomas 1992 sekaligus menamatkan penantian selama 25 tahun untuk merangkul kejuaraan itu adik-beradik Sidek terus berdedikasi terhadap pembangunan sukan negara sebagai jurulatih dan mentor yang disegani. Dalam peranan baharu itu, mereka akan berkongsi pengalaman serta meningkatkan kesedaranmengenai terapi sel stem Physoxic sebagai alternatif dalam pemulihan kecederaan dan juga pembedahan bagi kecederaan sukan. “Adik-beradik Sidek terus menyumbang kepada negara melalui usaha dan komitment mereka dalam pembangunan sukan badminton sebagai jurulatih dan mentor yang disegani. Pelantikan mereka sebagai Duta Testimoni MSC Physoxic Yakin mencerminkan nilai bersamadalam aspek kecemerlangan, ketahanan dan dedikasi dalam mengalakkan kesihatan serta kesejahteraan,” kata Datuk Steven Lai. Datuk Dr. Hj Mohmed Misbun berkata, setelah melalui sendiri cabaran dalam sukan berprestasi tinggi, beliau memahami kesan kecederaan terhadap seseorang atlet. “Kami berbangga dapat menyokong dan memperkenalkan terapi MSC Physoxic sebagai satu pilihan pemulihan yang berpotensi membantu atlet dan individu aktif pulih tanpa pembedahan,” katanya MoU dengan Auxi Therapeutics bagi Memajukan Operasi Makmal R&D GMP YAKIN MEDIC turut memeterai Memorandum Persefahaman (MoU) dengan Auxi Therapeutics bagi memperkukuh operasi makmal penyelidikan dan pembangunannya yang beroperasi mengikut piawaian Amalan Pengilangan Baik (GMP) di Pusat Perubatan Universiti Malaya (PPUM). MoU tersebut ditandatangani oleh Pengurus Besar Yakin Medic Sdn Bhd, Cik Charlize Tan dan Pengarah Auxi Therapeutics, Marina Choo. Dengan sokongan kerajaan Malaysia, Cik Charlize Tan berkata, makmal itu dijadualkan mula beroperasi dalam beberapa bulan akan datang, sekali gus menandakan satu pencapaian penting dalam landskap inovasi bioperubatan, imunologi dan terapi sel CAR-T di Malaysia. “Fasiliti ini meletakkan Malaysia di barisan hadapan dalam penyelidikan dan penghasilan sel stem. Menerusi usaha sama kami dengan Auxi Therapeutics, kami sedang membina sebuah pusat kecemerlangan serantau yang akan memacu inovasi dan menterjemahkan penemuan saintifik yang memberi manfaat kepada pesakit,” katanya. Cik Marina Choo memaklumkan, kerjasama itu akan menggabungkan penyelidikan saintifik kepakaran industri dan aplikasi dalam bidang kesihatan bagi memastikan hasil kajian di makmal dapat diterjemahkan kepada manfaat dan penyelesaian yang boleh digunakan dalam dunia sebenar. “Kerjasama ini menghubungkan bidang sains, industri dan penjagaan kesihatan dengan membawa hasil penyelidikan terkini kepada manfaat sebenar untuk pesakit. katanya. MoU dengan Vanfo Hino bagi Memajukan Operasi Makmal R&D GMP di Johor Bahru YAKIN MEDIC telah menandatangani MoU dengan Vanfo Hino Sdn Bhd bagi menubuhkan makmal pengkulturan MSC berstandard Amalan Pengilangan Baik (GMP) di Johor Bahru. Perjanjian tersebut ditandatangani oleh Cik Charlize Tan bagi pihak Yakin Medic Sdn Bhd dan Encik Zhang Wen bagi pihak Vanfo Hino Sdn Bhd. Fasiliti yang dicadangkan itu akan memenuhi keperluan pasaran di selatan Semenanjung Malaysia dan Singapura serta dilengkapi dengan teknologi bioreaktor termaju. YAKIN MEDIC berkata, makmal tersebut dijangka dapat memendekkan tempoh penghasilan, memperkemas logistik dan meningkatkan akses kepada produk MSC untuk menyediakan penjagaan kesihatan serta pesakit di rantau ini. Zhang Wen berkata, syarikat itu berbangga dapat bekerjasama dengan YAKIN MEDIC dalam membangunkan fasiliti strategik berkenaan. “Bersama-sama, kami akan menyediakan bekalan terapi MSC berkualiti tinggi yang konsisten dan tepat pada masanya, sekali gus menetapkan standard baharu bagi rantau ini,” katanya. Usaha Sama Sasar Pasaran Kesejahteraan Johor dan Singapura YAKIN turut bekerjasama dengan Axtra Health bagi menubuhkan sebuah usaha sama dalam perniagaan perubatan regeneratif di Johor Bahru. Perjanjian itu ditandatangani oleh Datuk Steven Lai dan Encik Soin Chee Kiong yang mewakili Axtra Health. Dengan memanfaatkan pengalaman luas kedua-dua organisasi dalam bidang bioteknologi dan perubatan regeneratif, entiti baharu itu menyasarkan untuk memenuhi keperluan pasaran Johor dan Singapura yang berkembang pesat. “Dengan menggabungkan kepimpinan saintifik YAKIN serta kepakaran Axtra Health dalam bidang kesihatan dan kesejahteraan, kami sedang mencipta sesuatu yang istimewa. Kerjasama ini akan membawa lebih banyak pilihan penjagaan kesihatan dan kesejahteraan yang inovatif serta membawa perubahan sebenar kepada kehidupan masyarakat,” kata Datuk Steven Lai. Saya balik rumah selepas kerja. “Saya juga antara orang yang jaga makan sebab ayah, ibu, adik dan kakak saya menghidap kencing manis. HAVANA: Cuba mene­gaskan tiada rundingan sedang berlangsung de­ngan Amerika Syarikat (AS) ketika pentadbiran Presiden Donald Trump meneruskan tekanan eko­nomi terhadap negara itu. Menteri Luar Cuba, Bruno Rodriguez berkata, Havana dan Washington tidak mengadakan rundingan serta tiada agenda untuk meneruskan perbincangan pada masa depan. Menurut kerajaan Cuba, sekatan berkenaan menyebabkan ekono­minya mengalami kerugian AS$8 bilion (RM32 bilion) antara Mac 2025 hingga Februari 2026. Jumlah itu merupakan angka kerugian tertinggi yang pernah direkodkan dan meningkat tujuh peratus berbanding tempoh laporan sebelum­nya. Rodriguez berkata, angka berkenaan tidak melibatkan beberapa se­katan terbaharu yang dikenakan Washington, termasuk terhadap bekalan tenaga Cuba pada Januari dan sekatan sekunder yang diper­kenalkan Mei lalu. Dalam hantaran di platform X, Rodriguez menyifatkan dasar itu sebagai ‘kelemahan ekonomi’ dan mendakwa sekatan AS yang telah lama menyebabkan kekurangan bekalan serta masalah ekonomi di Cuba sebagai tindakan ‘genosid’. “Sudah berbulan-bulan rakyat hanya mendapat bekalan elektrik selama dua atau tiga jam sehari atau kurang,” katanya sambil menggambarkan kesan buruk krisis tenaga yang me­runcing terhadap rakyat Cuba. – AGENSI

PROGRAM berteraskan Sains, Teknologi, Kejuruteraan dan Matematik (STEM) di luar bilik darjah bukan sahaja berjaya memupuk minat murid terhadap pembelajaran, malah selari dengan matlamat Kementerian Pendidikan Malaysia (KPM) untuk memperkukuh pendidikan STEM. Antaranya melahirkan murid yang berfikiran kritis, kreatif, inovatif serta berupaya mengaplikasikan pengetahuan dan kemahiran dalam menyelesaikan masalah kehidupan sebenar. Berbekalkan idea, konsep dan kreativiti, para pelajar memanfaatkan barangan terpakai untuk menghasilkan pelbagai rekaan inovatif. Pendekatan pembelajaran secara amali dan menyeronokkan itu, sekali gus memberi peluang kepada murid meneroka, mencuba dan mengembangkan potensi diri di luar bilik darjah. Buktinya, Model Demonstrasi Pergerakan Darah Dalam Jantung yang merupakan cetusan idea tiga pelajar tingkatan tiga Sekolah Agama Menengah (SAM) Hulu Langat ini berjaya mencuri tumpuan ramai menerusi kreativiti serta keupayaan mereka menterjemahkan konsep sains kepada sebuah model demonstrasi yang menarik. Mereka diwakili oleh Nik Aisy Adelia Nik Mohd Mujanif, Nur Adlin Humaira Mohd Nabil dan Alisha Sofiya Muhamad Khairul Nejam, yang menghasilkan model berkenaan bagi membantu murid memahami struktur dan proses peredaran darah dalam jantung dengan lebih mudah dan jelas. Nik Aisy Adelia berkata, tajuk tersebut dipilih berdasarkan bab tiga dalam silibus sains tingkatan tiga yang banyak menerangkan tentang struktur badan manusia. Katanya, murid sering menghadapi kesukaran untuk memahami struktur serta pergerakan darah dalam jantung kerana tidak dapat melihat proses tersebut secara visual, sekali gus menyukarkan mereka untuk membayangkan dan memahami topik berkenaan. “Model demonstrasi itu dihasilkan bagi memberikan kefahaman yang lebih mudah kepada murid melalui kaedah pembelajaran secara visual dan interaktif. Antara bahan yang digunakan untuk menghasilkan model tersebut ialah empat picagari, tiub serta gambar jantung,” katanya. Selain itu, ketiga-tiga pelajar itu turut menggunakan kaedah tapak tangan sebagai teknik mudah untuk membantu murid menghafal struktur jantung. Kaedah tersebut diharap dapat menjadikan proses pembelajaran lebih menarik dan mudah diingati. Mereka berpendapat murid pada masa kini lebih gemar belajar sambil bermain dan melakukan aktiviti interaktif berbanding hanya membaca buku teks semata-mata. Oleh itu, penggunaan model demonstrasi ini bukan sahaja dapat menarik minat murid, malah membantu mereka memahami topik sains dengan lebih berkesan. PEWANGI PANDAN MESRA ALAM Sekumpulan pelajar tingkatan satu menghasilkan inovasi Eco Scented Dehumidifier iaitu pewangi dan penyerap kelembapan berasaskan bahan semula jadi yang mudah didapati. Inovasi tersebut dihasilkan oleh Adelia Nur Hayfa Ahmad Husaini, Putri Nur Laila Sofia Mohammad Khairil dan Sufi Nur Amani Sahari. Adelia Nur Hayfa berkata, idea menghasilkan inovasi berkenaan tercetus daripada keinginan untuk menghasilkan pewangi yang lebih menjimatkan dan tahan lebih lama. Jelasnya, pewangi serta penyerap kelembapan yang dijual di pasaran kebiasannya lebih mahal dan hanya dapat digunakan dalam tempoh kira-kira seminggu. “Bagi mengatasi masalah tersebut, kami menggunakan bahan-bahan mudah didapati seperti daun pandan, garam kasar dan kepingan arang. “Daun pandan berfungsi memberikan aroma semula jadi yang menyenangkan manakala garam kasar membantu menyerap kelembapan dalam udara. Kepingan arang pula bertindak menyerap bau busuk, bau kepam serta kelembapan di dalam ruang tertutup. “Selain berfungsi sebagai pewangi, Eco Scented Dehumidifier juga dapat membantu mengurangkan bau tidak menyenangkan dan kelembapan, selain membantu menghalau serangga perosak seperti lipas. Aroma semula jadi daripada daun pandan turut memberikan kesegaran kepada ruang tertutup,” katanya. Menariknya, inovasi tersebut mampu bertahan sehingga dua bulan berbanding pewangi komersial yang biasanya perlu diganti dalam tempoh lebih singkat. Penggunaan bahan yang mudah diperoleh juga menjadikan inovasi ini lebih praktikal dan menjimatkan. Melalui penghasilan Eco Scented Dehumidifier, ketiga-tiga pelajar itu berharap inovasi berasaskan bahan semula jadi ini dapat menjadi alternatif yang mudah, murah dan mesra alam untuk kegunaan di rumah. RODA SEJARAH Sekumpulan pelajar Tingkatan Tiga, Khairun Nadiah Jamzuri, Irina Yasmin Zuwardi Azer dan Muhammad Hadif Ilmi Jawadi menghasilkan satu alat inovasi pembelajaran yang diberi nama Roda Sejarah atau History Wheel bagi menjadikan subjek Sejarah lebih menarik dan interaktif. Menurut mereka, idea menghasilkan inovasi tersebut tercetus apabila mendapati kebanyakan murid mudah berasa bosan dengan subjek Sejarah yang mengandungi terlalu banyak perkataan dan fakta untuk dibaca serta diingati. Keadaan itu turut menyebabkan murid sukar memberikan tumpuan dalam tempoh yang lama. Justeru, Khairun Naidah berkata, Roda Sejarah dihasilkan sebagai kaedah pembelajaran yang dapat membantu murid mengingat fakta dengan lebih cepat melalui pendekatan yang menyeronokkan dan interaktif. “Objektif utama inovasi tersebut adalah untuk menjadikan Sejarah sebagai subjek yang tidak membosankan, selain membantu murid memahami serta mengingati fakta dengan lebih mudah. “Inovasi berkenaan merangkumi enam aspek penting dalam pembelajaran Sejarah iaitu tokoh, tarikh, peristiwa, sebab, kesan dan pengajaran. Keenam-enam aspek tersebut disusun dalam Roda Sejarah bagi memudahkan murid membuat ulang kaji secara lebih tersusun,” katanya. Roda Sejarah dihasilkan menggunakan bahan yang mudah didapati dan sebahagian daripadanya berasaskan bahan kitar semula seperti kotak, kad manila, kertas warna, straw serta bahan hiasan lain. Penggunaan bahan tersebut bukan sahaja menjadikan inovasi lebih menjimatkan malah menerapkan elemen kreativiti dalam kalangan pelajar. Cara penggunaannya juga mudah. Murid terlebih dahulu membaca dan memahami topik Sejarah berdasarkan enam aspek yang disediakan. Selepas itu, murid perlu mencabut satu nombor secara rawak daripada sebuah bekas sebelum memusingkan Roda Sejarah. Apabila roda berhenti, murid perlu menjawab soalan berdasarkan nombor yang dipilih dan bahagian yang diperoleh pada roda tersebut. Kaedah ini menjadikan proses pembelajaran seperti satu permainan, sekali gus dapat menarik perhatian murid dan menggalakkan mereka terlibat secara aktif. Melalui penghasilan Roda Sejarah, ketiga-tiga pelajar berharap subjek Sejarah dapat dipelajari dengan cara yang lebih menyeronokkan, interaktif dan mudah diingat sekali gus membantu murid meningkatkan minat serta kefahaman terhadap subjek tersebut. STATUS BUKAN HALANGAN Walaupun berstatus Sekolah Agama Bantuan Kerajaan (SABK), ia bukan halangan buat SAM Hulu Langat menganjurkan program STEM. STEM Explore 2026 yang dianjurkan buat kali kedua di sekolah yang tertubuh sejak 1983 itu, menepis stigma terhadap fungsi sekolah agama yang hanya menekankan subjek berteraskan dini (keagamaan) dan Bahasa Arab. Kali pertama dianjurkan pada 2024, program yang melibatkan penyertaan pelajar menengah rendah dari tingkatan satu hingga tiga memberi fokus kepada penghasilan inovasi dan kreativiti dalam kalangan murid. Tahun ini, program itu diteruskan dengan pengisian yang lebih berfokus kepada inovasi bagi memberi peluang kepada murid menghasilkan produk serta mengembangkan kemahiran berfikir secara kreatif. Pengetua SAM Hulu Langat, Mahani Othman, berkata, aktiviti yang dilaksanakan bukan sekadar menghasilkan sesuatu produk, sebaliknya turut membantu murid membina pelbagai kemahiran sosial dan kemahiran menyelesaikan masalah. “Daripada satu tugasan yang mudah seperti menyediakan jambatan, sebenarnya murid dapat mengembangkan banyak kemahiran sosial apabila mereka berhubung dan bekerjasama dengan rakan untuk menyelesaikan sesuatu masalah sehingga akhirnya berjaya menghasilkan jambatan mengikut spesifikasi yang ditetapkan,” katanya. Antara aktiviti yang dianjurkan sepanjang program dua hari itu termasuk pertandingan inovasi dan reka cipta, pertandingan membina jambatan, cabaran kereta lumba, pameran terrarium STEM, cabaran kalkulator dan mini zoo bergerak. Mahani berkata, pendekatan sedemikian dapat melahirkan kemahiran mencipta dan menggalakkan murid berfikir secara kreatif, selaras keperluan pendidikan semasa yang memberi penekanan terhadap pembentukan murid yang mempunyai daya pemikiran kreatif dan inovatif. “Program berkenaan turut melibatkan penghasilan dan pameran daripada beberapa panitia termasuk Panitia Sains, Reka Bentuk dan Teknologi (RBT), Fizik serta beberapa mata pelajaran lain. “Pada tahun ini, program turut diperkasakan menerusi sinergi bersama rakan strategik dan komuniti sekolah di sekeliling,” katanya. LET’S READ SUARA SARAWAK/ NEW SARAWAK TRIBUNE E-PAPER FOR FREE AS ​​EARLY AS 2 AM EVERY DAY. CLICK LINK The second part of this two-part series explores why digital literacy goes beyond knowing how to use technology, highlighting the importance of critical thinking, healthy boundaries and parental guidance in helping children navigate an increasingly AI-driven world. From Screen Users to Digital Thinkers In a world where information and technology are expanding at an unprecedented pace, children are growing up at the centre of the digital age. With much of how they learn, communicate and discover the world now shaped by technology, digital literacy is no longer an optional skill but an essential one that should be developed from a young age. Literacy is no longer confined to the ability to read and write. Digital literacy also means knowing how to access, understand, evaluate and use information responsibly in an increasingly digital world. Teacher and co-founder of The Learning Curve, Kenneth Chai, said digital literacy is not necessarily determined by age, but by a person’s understanding of the digital environment. “My eight-year-old can recognise an advertisement on the internet almost immediately, while my father may not necessarily recognise that something is advertising or trying to influence him,” Chai said, giving an example. For Chai, this highlights why digital literacy goes beyond simply knowing how to operate a device. “It is about understanding the digital environment around us; who is trying to influence us, what information we can trust, how technology works, and how we can use it to solve problems rather than simply consume content,” he added. But digital technology is not something we can avoid or shield ourselves from. With our growing dependence on the digital world, it has become an integral part of our lives — and our children’s lives — shaping how they learn, communicate, work and eventually make decisions. “We are entering a generation where AI-generated content, AI-assisted work and digital environments will simply be normal. Like it or not, our children will grow up surrounded by these technologies,” said Chai. He believes that if children cannot understand and navigate the digital world they live in, they may eventually become a different kind of illiterate. Knowing does not mean understanding As an educator, Chai has seen many children who are skilled at using technology, but that does not necessarily mean they understand it. A child might know how to use TikTok, YouTube or ChatGPT, for instance, but may not understand what lies beyond simply operating these platforms. “Do they understand why certain content is appearing in front of them? Do they know when something is an advertisement, misinformation or AI-generated content? Do they understand what happens to their data?” he asked. This is particularly important as children are exposed to an overwhelming amount of information online. “The challenge is no longer finding information. We have almost unlimited information available to us. The challenge is knowing what to trust, what to question and what needs further investigation,” he said. With the rise of artificial intelligence, the ability to question and verify information has become even more crucial. Children will increasingly encounter AI-generated content, misinformation and what is now commonly referred to as “AI slop”. With the right guidance, children can use AI as a tool to enhance learning and develop their skills. Chai believes they should be taught to look beyond what is presented to them and ask: “Who created this? Why was it created? Where did this information come from? Can I verify it somewhere else?” The goal, he stressed, is not to make children distrust everything, but to encourage them to think critically. This ability to think critically also extends to how children use technology itself. “Technology can either make children think less or help them think better. It depends entirely on how we design and use it,” Chai said. He pointed to artificial intelligence as an example, noting that the same technology that allows a student to finish homework in minutes can also analyse examination papers, identify weak areas, create visual explanations and develop personalised study plans. “The technology itself is not the problem. The question is: are we teaching children to use it to finish their homework faster, or to solve problems and learn better?” To Chai, any cutting-edge technology is a double-edged sword, which means it is the adults’ responsibility to teach children how to use it wisely. Digital literacy starts young Digital literacy needs to be taught as early as possible, particularly as children are already exposed to technology from a very young age. However, Chai stressed that early digital literacy does not mean giving young children unlimited access to devices. He said unrestricted access can be harmful and that children need clear boundaries around their use of digital devices. “Today, many children have unlimited data, unlimited screen time and unrestricted access to the internet. But constraints are actually where problem-solving begins,” said Chai. “It can start with conversations: What is this advertisement? Who made this video? Should we trust this information? Why is this game trying to get us to buy something?” he added. Every child, however, is different, growing up in environments shaped by their parents, siblings and surroundings. Chai said his own children have been exposed to technology from a young age, but are also aware of their restrictions, screen time and available resources. “Most importantly, I try to stay involved. I don’t think there is a universal formula. What matters is intentional exposure, appropriate boundaries and active parental involvement,” he said. With proper guidance, children can become digitally literate from a young age. “Give a child limited resources and watch them plan. Give them a budget and let them decide what they want to spend it on. Give them boundaries and let them learn how to work within those boundaries,” he added. Technology should be treated in much the same way. Instead of unlimited access, Chai advocates intentional access. Rather than allowing technology to give children every answer immediately, parents and educators should create experiences that require them to think, plan and make decisions. “Sometimes constraints can become a form of parenting currency. Children learn that access, resources and privileges come with responsibility,” he said. For parents, setting boundaries does not mean having to become technology experts. Chai believes the most important thing is involvement — talking to children about what they are doing online, asking about the tools they use and, where possible, learning alongside them. “Ask them to show you what they are using. Ask them why they like it. Ask them to teach you. Have conversations,” he said. He also cautioned against creating a divide where children feel their parents cannot understand the technology they use. While parents may not always be familiar with every new platform or tool, Chai said curiosity and openness can help keep the conversation going. “I may not understand every new technology they use in the future — and honestly, they may eventually know more about certain technologies than I do. But I never want them to feel that they cannot talk to me about it,” he added. For Chai, keeping that conversation open is just as important as setting boundaries. Ultimately, children need to develop their own judgement and learn to make responsible decisions both online and offline. Preparing children for a digital world Daunting and filled with potential dangers, the digital world can nevertheless transform the way children learn and prepare for the future. The technology we use today may become obsolete by the time children enter the workforce, and they may find themselves using entirely different tools. Chai said children should therefore be taught not just how to use a particular app, but how to understand, evaluate and adapt to new technologies. To do so, they need skills in critical thinking, information literacy, AI literacy, digital security and privacy awareness. “Not to forget creativity, communication and problem-solving. Hence, I personally encourage parents not to simply prohibit AI. “In fact, we often encourage parents to explore LLMs and AI tools with their children. It is better for children to learn now under guidance and supervision than to be completely overwhelmed by these technologies in the future.” However, careful implementation is still needed in a world where possibilities exist at every turn. Used in a controlled environment, technology can be life-changing. “Used poorly, they can also create dependency, misinformation and inequality,” he said. At The Learning Curve, Chai and his team are working to build a parenting community that encourages more conversations about digital literacy. They have also created Spark, an AI learning platform designed as a two-way learning tool where AI does not replace teachers and parents, but works alongside them. With the right guidance, children can use AI as a tool to enhance learning and develop their skills. Ultimately, the goal is not to raise children who simply know how to operate the latest device or navigate the newest platform. It is to raise children who can question what they see, understand the technology they use, make informed decisions and use digital tools to create rather than merely consume. As technology continues to evolve, the definition of literacy will continue to expand with it. For today’s children, being literate may mean more than knowing how to read the words on a page — it may also mean knowing how to read the world behind a screen. And perhaps, in preparing children for an increasingly digital future, the greatest skill we can give them is not knowing every technology, but knowing how to think. Setiausaha Perbendaharaan AS, Scott Bessent, berikrar bahawa AS akan mengisytiharkan ‘Hari Penentuan Ekonomi” terhadap Iran, dengan berjanji untuk menyekat sumber kewangan negara tersebut. “Di bawah Operasi Economic Outcast, kami telah berjanji untuk mengenakan tindakan tegas terhadap mereka yang menyediakan sokongan kewangan kepada rejim Iran,” kata Bessent. Beliau memberi amaran mana-mana pihak yang menjalankan urusan dengan syarikat penerbangan Iran yang masih beroperasi berdepan risiko disekat daripada sistem kewangan global. Selain syarikat penerbangan Iran, Jabatan Perbendaharaan AS berkata, tindakan terbaharunya turut menyasarkan firma di negara ketiga yang memudahkan aktiviti Mahan Air yang dikenakan sekatan AS, operasi penerbangan yang mempunyai kaitan dengan keganasan serta pemerolehan haram pesawat buatan AS. Jabatan itu turut menyasarkan penyedia perkhidmatan kargo dan ejen jualan am yang mengendalikan penerbangan antarabangsa Mahan Air. Mahan Air ialah syarikat penerbangan Iran yang didakwa membantu melancarkan aktiviti Kor Pengawal Revolusi Islam Iran (IRGC). Pegawai Jabatan Perbendaharaan AS itu tidak menjelaskan sama ada firma di negara seperti China mungkin dikenakan sekatan sekunder kerana menyokong sektor penerbangan Iran, namun berkata, Washington mempunyai pelbagai pilihan tindakan terhadap penyedia perkhidmatan. She has ballet at 11am, arts class at 1pm and music lesson at 3pm. I have to get up and get them ready for their classes.” Are your kids constantly transiting between classes? Taekwondo, music classes, math classes, football practices and the list goes on. It is undeniable that structured out of school activities are beneficial for your kids. It is always a dilemma for parents to keep a balanced schedule for their kids while not wanting their kids to miss out in their academic or general development. But in your rush to give them the best of both, are you overscheduling your kids? If you’re not sure, learn more about the pros and cons, and find out how you can strike a balance. You’re probably overscheduling your child if: • He is eating one to many drive-thru meals or surviving on bread alone. • He is doing his homework in the car in between classes. • He lacks proper rest. A child below 10 requires at least 10 hours of sleep. • He falls sick often. • He is tired, unmotivated and burnt out. • He is missing out on normal childhood activities such as birthdays, visiting his grandparents, or lacks time for unstructured play. Striking a balance While working out a balance between structured activities and unstructured activities isn’t rocket science, it will require communication between you and your children. Arrange for the whole family to sit down for a family discussion on how you can achieve a balance. Here are some items that you should consider: 1. Find out what activities your child likes. If there are free trial classes, let him try it out, especially during long school breaks. This gives him more time to explore his passions without pressure. 2. Be aware of your child’s strengths and difficulties. When he comes home happy after an activity, it is a sign that he enjoys it. Discuss his development with the programme providers and decide if you should continue the class. 3. Learning doesn’t stop in the classroom. Make time for your child so that he can apply what he has learnt at school, e.g. get him to help out with measuring things while you are doing some DIY work at home, weighing out ingredients while cooking, teaching him about plants while gardening or grocery shopping, etc. 4. Get involved in his homework by providing him with guidance. However, this does not mean that you should do his homework for him! Be patient as it may take some time. 5. Carve out family time doing things that he likes. 6. Ensure that he has at least an hour a day to just play. Children learn best through play and unstructured play will help him to explore his own creativity and problemsolving skills. 7. Ensure there’s a balance between outdoor exercises and indoor activities. 8. Sleep is important for a growing child. Make sure that he is in bed by 9pm every night! When customers initiate a payment through CIMB Clicks Web or an online merchant site, a SecureTAC push notification will be sent to their primary phone. They can tap the notification or open the SecureTAC menu in the OCTO app to review the transaction before selecting “Approve”. The app will then require Face ID, fingerprint scanning or the six-digit OCTO App passcode before the payment can proceed. Customers who have not set up any of these security features can still initiate transactions and receive SecureTAC notifications. However, attempting to approve a transaction will trigger an error and the payment will be rejected until biometric authentication or an OCTO App passcode has been configured. The six-digit passcode serves as a fallback when biometric verification is unavailable, including when a fingerprint scanner fails or facial authentication cannot be completed. It is configured separately within the OCTO app and is different from both the customer’s phone screen lock and CIMB Clicks password. Cancelling the authentication prompt or repeatedly entering an incorrect passcode will also result in the transaction being rejected. CIMB said unsuccessful SecureTAC approvals will not lock a customer’s CIMB Clicks ID and no money will be deducted from the account. Customers are advised to check their OCTO app security settings before retrying a failed payment and to contact CIMB’s support centre if problems persist after a second attempt. Despite those constraints, demand remained active, particularly among first-time buyers and young families. Jan said affordable single- and double-storey landed homes continued to be the preferred choice for many local purchasers. “People generally like having their own land, car porch and more space for the family,” he said. However, condominiums and apartments were also drawing enquiries from younger purchasers, investors and those seeking homes closer to the city. Ahmad Farhan said terrace houses remained popular because of their space and privacy, although buyers were increasingly willing to consider high-rise units when they offered better locations and more manageable repayments. Jan said buyers had become more price-sensitive compared with 2025, but their decisions were increasingly based on value rather than simply finding the lowest price. “They are looking for value for money. For most first-time buyers, the priorities are monthly instalments and overall price, followed by location and the size or practicality of the house,” he said. Timberland Group of Companies sales administration manager Sherry Jee similarly identified price as the first filter for purchasers. “If a property exceeds their budget, location becomes irrelevant. Second to price is location, followed closely by architectural design,” she said. Jee said investors generally preferred prime urban locations with rental potential, while owner-occupiers focused more on practical layouts and functional living spaces. Landed developments in Moyan, Matang and Serian were attracting growing families seeking more space, larger parking areas and higher ceilings. High-rise projects, meanwhile, appealed more to young professionals, smaller families and investors who valued accessibility and integrated facilities. Projects near proposed Autonomous Rapid Transit (ART) routes, Universiti Malaysia Sarawak (UNIMAS) and upcoming healthcare facilities were also receiving encouraging interest because of their connectivity and potential for long-term appreciation. Buyers in their late 20s to late 30s, particularly Millennials purchasing their first homes, made up a substantial share of enquiries, while Gen Z purchasers were beginning to enter the market. However, many younger Gen Z buyers remained in the research and financial-planning stage as they built their careers and savings. Jan said younger buyers often researched market prices, financing, locations and competing projects online before speaking to an agent. Developers were responding by offering more compact units, practical layouts and incentives including rebates, furnishing packages, legal-fee assistance and lower initial entry costs. Sustainability features such as solar panels, EV charging facilities and energy-efficient designs were also attracting greater interest, although buyers generally remained unwilling to pay a substantial premium for them. “The market is not against sustainability. Buyers want to know how much extra they must pay and what they will receive in return, whether in the short or long term,” Jan said. Jee said EV charging stations were becoming an industry trend developers needed to prepare for, although they remained an added advantage rather than a deciding factor for buyers. HAMILTON (Canada), Sept 9 (Bernama-Anadolu) -- The 81st session of the UN General Assembly opened on Tuesday with President Khalilur Rahman calling for renewed efforts to restore trust in multilateralism, as UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that rebuilding confidence in the global system is "the defining challenge of our time", Anadolu Ajansi reported. Rahman said the UN's endurance over eight decades speaks to its core purpose, noting "for more than eight decades, our organisation has helped the world avoid plunging into a third world war, arguably the very reason for its existence." Highlighting the often unseen work of the UN, he said, "every day, often far from the spotlight, the United Nations and its dedicated corps of professionals work to feed millions of people, including refugees and other displaced populations around the world, support peace and security, combat chronic diseases, and help countries address complex transboundary challenges." Rahman also acknowledged the institution has repeatedly failed to meet expectations, noting the conflicts, fragile development gains and worsening climate impacts. "Conflicts continue to inflict immense human suffering, development gains remain feeble and fragile, climate impacts are intensifying," he said. Warning that these compounding crises have eroded faith in collective action, he said, "a widening trust deficit is testing confidence in international institutions and collective action, a deficit that we must close by working together through dialogue, renewed cooperation, and delivery." Google to invest €13bil in AI infrastructure in Finland

Google said the investments also covered 'clean energy projects and dedicated nature and community funds to support local biodiversity, education, research, and workforce development'. (EPA Images pic)
HELSINKI: Google said Wednesday that it would invest at least €13 billion (US$15 billion) in digital infrastructure, including data centres to power artificial intelligence models, in Finland over the next two years.
"This is Google's largest single investment in Europe and a testament to Finland's leadership in responsibly building AI infrastructure," the company said in a statement, adding that the investments included "clean energy projects".
The investment includes data centres and supporting infrastructure as well as partnerships in the municipalities of Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala.
The infrastructure would power several of the tech giant's services, including its AI chatbot Gemini.
Google said the investments also covered "clean energy projects, and dedicated nature and community funds to support local biodiversity, education, research, and workforce development".
"Google's decision is a clear testament to our strengths. The value of the data economy extends far beyond direct investment into spurring innovation, research and development," Finland's Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said in Google's statement.
"Deepening our collaboration with Google will deliver lasting benefits for both parties," he added.
Since buying a former paper mill and transforming it into a data centre in the coastal city of Hamina in 2009, Google has gradually increased its presence in the country.
The construction phase of the new investments is expected in 2027 and 2028, and Google estimated it would boost Finland's GDP by €3.6 billion annually and "support more than 37,000 jobs" across the Nordic country.
An estimated 16,000 of these jobs will be in the construction sector.
After the construction phase, the running of the "digital infrastructure" will support around 7,000 jobs annually, including "on-site facility and technical roles, upstream suppliers of equipment and services, and the local shops, restaurants and amenities supported by these workers and their families".
With its cool climate and relatively stable and cheap electricity thanks to nuclear plants as well as extensive wind and hydro power, Finland has seen a boom in data centres in recent years, with dozens already under construction.
Attracting investments in the sector has been a priority for Orpo's right-wing government as the Nordic country grapples with record-high unemployment and sluggish economic growth.

Umno’s 2026 general assembly should be judged less by which coalition it prefers than by whether the party can prove that participation in government has made it more useful to voters.
The real test is converting access to power into public confidence before the 16th general election.
The assembly, running from Sept 9 to 12, brings together more than 6,400 delegates. Umno secretary-general Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki has said 157 motions from divisions include the party’s political direction and cooperation within the unity government.
Delegates are, therefore, examining whether Umno’s present arrangement strengthens its claim to represent Malay interests while governing a plural country.
That distinction matters. Since GE15 produced a hung Parliament, Umno has operated within a coalition it once opposed electorally. The arrangement helped provide federal stability, but stability alone cannot rebuild political loyalty. Malay voters who moved elsewhere did not necessarily abandon Umno because of one coalition formula. Their decisions also reflected leadership credibility, governance, economic pressure and responsiveness to everyday concerns.
This makes the debate over staying in or leaving the unity government incomplete. Coalition arithmetic is important, but changing partners cannot substitute for rebuilding trust.
Barisan Nasional secretary-general Zambry Abdul Kadir has reaffirmed the coalition’s commitment to maintaining the government until an election is called, even as Umno leaders discuss the merits of an earlier GE16. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said an earlier election can be considered while stressing economic recovery, public welfare and combating corruption.
Umno, therefore, faces two responsibilities simultaneously. It must preserve enough political independence to remain recognisable to its traditional base while demonstrating that its role in government contributes to national stability and effective administration. If it appears merely attached to federal power, it risks losing identity. If it pursues confrontation simply to display independence, it risks weakening the stability it helped create.
The stronger route is performance politics.
For voters, coalition arguments eventually collide with household economics. Wages, food costs, housing, employment opportunities, education and social mobility shape political confidence more directly than elite negotiations.
The pre-assembly Malay Education Convention, where Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi outlined goals linking Bumiputera education more closely with recognised industrial competencies and workplace learning, points toward a more durable political language: measurable advancement rather than symbolic reassurance.
But announcements require accountability. Umno should use its position in government to demonstrate outcomes that can be independently assessed: skills pathways, employment prospects, assistance for vulnerable households, transparent administration and opportunities for younger Malays without framing national prosperity as a zero-sum ethnic contest. Malay advancement and an inclusive Malaysian economy need not be competing objectives.
The assembly also presents a leadership test. Zahid described the 2026 general assembly as a forum for delegates to bring the voices and responsibilities of the grassroots. That principle carries consequences. If grassroots concerns are genuinely central, uncomfortable views about alliances, leadership, candidate quality and government performance must be heard rather than converted into ceremonial consensus.
GE16 preparation should consequently begin with candidate credibility and constituency intelligence, not slogans. Umno’s machinery remains an organisational advantage, but machinery cannot manufacture trust indefinitely. Candidates must possess local legitimacy, clean reputations, policy competence and the ability to communicate across generations. Younger voters inhabit a political environment where information travels instantly and institutional loyalty cannot be assumed.
Umno should also confront an evidence gap. Public claims about a return of Malay confidence require constituency-level proof. Electoral gains, membership enthusiasm and crowded political gatherings measure different things.
The party needs analysis of voter transferability, turnout, age cohorts, marginal constituencies and reasons voters change allegiance. Without such evidence, optimism can become strategy by anecdote.
This year's Umno general assembly, therefore, matters not because it can settle Umno’s future in four days, but because it can clarify the standard by which that future should be measured. The question is not whom Umno stands beside, but what it delivers.
Beyond the assembly, its renewal will depend on turning relevance into governing usefulness. If Umno can connect Malay confidence with competent administration, economic opportunity, institutional integrity and national stability, it can approach GE16 with a defensible proposition.
If coalition positioning remains the main story, the party may leave Kuala Lumpur more united internally without becoming more persuasive electorally.

Azam Mohd is an FMT reader.

Billionaire Korean gamer hit by record US$1.9 bil divorce bill

(Sept 9): A South Korean court ordered the billionaire founder of gaming giant Smilegate to pay his wife a settlement of 2.55 trillion won (US$1.9 billion or RM7.8 billion) including handing over 35% of the company, setting the stage for the country’s biggest divorce ever. Kwon Hyuk-bin owns 100% of Smilegate, the studio behind blockbuster shooting game Crossfire and role-playing title Lost Ark . He founded it in 2002, a year after getting married to Lee Hwa-jin, who initiated legal proceedings for the divorce. The Seoul Family Court on Wednesday ordered Kwon to give Lee a 35% stake in the company, a court spokesperson confirmed. The court has assessed the value of Kwon’s Smilegate stake at around 7.1 trillion won. It additionally ordered a cash payment of 65 billion won. If finalised, this would overshadow the 944 billion won the Seoul High Court recently ordered SK Group chairman Chey Tae-won to pay his ex-wife in their divorce case, which he is appealing. Both Kwon and Lee can still challenge the Wednesday ruling. The court proceedings were closed, and the parties’ filings and the appraisal report were not publicly available. A law firm representing Kwon declined to comment. Lawyers for Lee could not immediately be reached for comment. The verdict could reshape ownership of one of the country’s largest private firms. Previously, the Bloomberg Billionaires Index had estimated the 52-year-old Kwon’s fortune to be US$3 billion (RM12.2 billion). The Smilegate case “is significant because it concerns how to assess a spouse’s contribution to a business established and developed during the marriage”, said Woongkyu Cho, a partner at Barun Law specialising in inheritance and business succession. “This case may provide guidance on how courts value homemaking and childcare that enable the other spouse to concentrate on building a business and accumulating substantial wealth,” Cho added. Lee has previously held executive positions at the company, according to an official registry document obtained by Bloomberg . Smilegate said in a statement earlier this year that all of the initial capital for the company came from Kwon, although Lee held a 30% stake when the company was founded. According to the company, Lee did not work at the office and did not have a desk at the firm. Uploaded by Chng Shear Lane
Diesel crunch threatens lasting price pain, consumption cutbacks

(Sept 9): The global refining sector’s diesel crunch is likely to result in tight supply for the coming months, keeping prices high and weighing on demand, according to analysts and traders. On top of more than six months of war in the Persian Gulf, impeding output there — and a fresh flare-up over recent days — the market is contending with the impact of Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries, which have prompted the country to extend a ban on diesel exports. Fuel exports lost from the major processing hubs in the Middle East and Russia now amount to two million barrels a day each, Vitol Group’s CEO Russell Hardy told the Asia Pacific Petroleum Conference run by S&P Global Energy in Singapore. With refiners elsewhere already at their limit, consumers have turned to distillate fuel stockpiles and will keep drawing. “We’re still not running enough refining capacity to prevent those draws,” he said. The price of diesel — known as the workhorse fuel of the global economy — has run ahead of crude since the start of the war, with the jump in the ICE gasoil benchmark more than twice that seen for Brent, creating inflationary pressures even while oil has remained relatively stable. Crude prices are now also running toward US$100 for the first time since July. In the US, retail diesel has hit records above a former peak set in June 2022. Eye-watering diesel margins have incentivised refiners outside Russia and the Middle East to run hard to capture gains but the clock is ticking on how long they can keep up the feat. Refinery equipment gets increasingly vulnerable to breakdowns if operated at high utilisation rates for too long. That could mean an outage at a time where buffers are limited, exacerbating the crisis. “If we can sustain until the end of this year, it is going to be an achievement,” Shaikh Khaled Al-Sabah, managing director for international marketing at Kuwait Petroleum Corp, said of the global refining system. That creates the risk of “a huge shortage that’s going to be seen quite soon” in fuels, he added. US exports have helped alleviate tightness, particularly in import-dependent Europe. But that may not hold as diesel consumption there begins to increase as temperatures drop, given the US is not producing more, even as shipments have climbed. “I think we’re going to see a very difficult winter coming in Northwest Europe,” said KPC’s Al-Sabah. “This is only the beginning.” Uploaded by Arion Yeow
Policeman kills teacher wife at Thai school, kids safe: officials

BANGKOK: A police officer shot dead his teacher wife at the kindergarten where she worked in Thailand on Wednesday (Sept 9) but all the children are safe, officials said. The gunman returned home after the shooting in Chonburi province, south-east of Bangkok, where police were negotiating his surrender. The incident is the latest shooting to rock Thailand, a month after a teenager shot his grandparents and then five staff and a pupil at his school, before killing himself. Thailand has one of the highest rates of gun ownership in the region, and past promises of tightening gun laws have not prevented repeated shootings. Sayan Klomaon, chairman of Nong Pla Lai sub-district council, said the gunman - a policeman local to the area - came to the school at about 10:30 am (0330 GMT) and talked with his wife before shooting her. No students saw the incident, as it happened outside the classroom, he said, adding that the gunman then left to go home, and since then all the children had been picked up. In a statement on Facebook, Chonburi Governor Naris Niramaiwong confirmed that all 44 children were safely evacuated along with three teachers and three other staff members. He said police had surrounded the house where the gunman was and were negotiating his surrender. The motive remains unclear. Naris ordered the kindergarten closed and said psychological support will be provided to children and staff who witnessed the incident. In 2022, an ex-policeman armed with a gun and a knife stormed a nursery in northern Thailand and killed 24 children and 12 adults, in one of the country's deadliest massacres. - AFP Follow us on our official WhatsApp channel for breaking news alerts and key updates! China’s memories of Mao shift with the times, 50 years after his death

A propaganda mural on a street in Zhoujiazhuang Commune, Jinzhou, in northern China’s Hebei province. Photo: AFP The crimson flags on Nanjie village's "East is Red" Square hang limp in the sweltering summer heat as a trickle of tourists take photos with a towering statue of Chairman Mao Zedong, still gleaming white almost 50 years after he died. The Great Helmsman, who died on Sept 9, 1976, is still very much a fixture in central Henan province's Nanjie – often dubbed "China's last Maoist village". Nostalgia for Mao's egalitarian ideals is growing in China as memories of his turbulent rule fade and the country grapples with a slowing economy and inequality. Mao, who led the 1949 communist revolution against the ruling nationalists, ushered in an era of collectivised ownership he argued would drive industry and unite the country, but his drastic policies are also blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths. While the ruling Chinese Communist Party maintains Mao was a revolutionary hero, it publicly acknowledged after his death that his devastating Cultural Revolution was a "grave mistake" – a verdict upheld by subsequent leaders. In Nanjie, countless murals of the former Chinese leader are plastered around the village. Residents still live under Maoist principles of shared ownership, while the rest of the country moved on from that economic model. A vendor displays souvenirs featuring late Communist leader Mao Zedong and other Chinese leaders at a shop in Dazhai, northern China’s Shanxi province. Photo: AFP "I still revere him very much," Xie Kaiyue, a 22-year-old local university student, said of Mao, who died almost three decades before she was born. "I think young people in the village and, actually, myself, aren't as strong-spirited as in the past ... people were purer," she said. Nearby, electric carts whisked visitors past uniform apartment blocks plastered with socialist slogans as guides explained how cooperative ownership in local enterprises funds free housing for residents. Party line Around 500km north, in the mountain village of Dazhai in Shanxi province, once promoted by Mao as a national model after locals terraformed its arid hills into irrigated fields, tourists reminisce about an era when the Great Helmsman dominated political and social life. "(People) didn't have enough to eat or to wear," Li, a 64-year-old tourist from Xi'an, said of his childhood. "But ... the whole country was full of vigour, and there was a spirit of struggling with heaven, earth, and people to change every aspect of China," the retiree said. "Of course I miss it." Now, Dazhai is overflowing with shops selling items that support Mao's personality cult – posters, playing cards, and crockery emblazoned with his image, and the "Little Red Book" of his quotations. Still, references to dark chapters of his decades in absolute power are tightly censored in public discourse. A staff member cleans the floor of an exhibition hall at the Dazhai Museum in Dazhai, northern China’s Shanxi province. Photo: AFP The decade-long episode instigated by Mao in 1966 saw intellectuals brutally targeted as "class enemies" and schools shuttered, setting China back for years in education and development. Private property and land were collectivised, while economic management pushed the country to the Great Famine, which the government says killed around 15 million people, while historians estimate around 20-43 million. In one museum, text mentioning the Cultural Revolution had been crudely scraped off signage. "Everything you see in the public domain ... is the party line. No one is allowed to deviate from this," said scholar Xu Chenggang, who was targeted as a child in Beijing during the Cultural Revolution because his father was labelled a "rightist". Mao's face is printed on banknotes, his portrait overlooks Tiananmen Square, and his body is preserved in a mausoleum. Every year new movies and TV shows dramatising Mao's life beam the message of his great deeds to public. Public discussion has been squeezed further under current leader Xi Jinping, who warns against "historical nihilism", or narratives contradicting the party's own. "The Communist Party told people there were mistakes, but what's the meaning of 'mistake'? No one knows," Xu said. 'Great figure' The sanitised history has left space for romanticised interpretations among youths frustrated by long working hours and intense competition in education and the job market. In December, a viral video series on Bilibili – a platform popular with those under 30 – argued that the 2017 movie Youth, which follows young performers in a military dance troupe during the 1970s, was a subtle ode to the Cultural Revolution. A man walks past a statue of Mao Zedong at the cultural centre in Zhoujiazhuang Commune, Jinzhou, northern China’s Hebei province. Photo: AFP The videos, which praised Mao and blamed capitalist elites for crushing the movement, were removed after gaining over 35 million views in less than a week. "Today, there is more of a sense that the Cultural Revolution was a period of idealism, where society was fired by ideals and not by the relentless pursuit of money and material goods," said to Kerry Brown, head of the Lau China Institute in London and author of a recent book on Mao. "This is, of course, a total fabrication," he said. Many also credit Mao with laying the foundation for China to become a modern, technologically advanced nation, said Mobo Gao, professor of Chinese studies at Adelaide University. "They ask, where did (today's China) come from? It came from the establishment of the PRC," said Gao, who lived through the Mao era in rural Jiangxi province. "Who was the one who really established the PRC? It must be Mao." In Shijiazhuang, an industrial city of seven million northeast of Dazhai, 20-year-old Wang Zhihao and his classmates posed with a giant Mao statue opposite the municipal government. "We admire and revere Chairman Mao very much. He is a great figure," said Wang, as the sound of elderly residents singing songs praising the Communist Party drifted over from the nearby square.
