Hun Manet instructs halt to sand dredging near erosion sites, orders inspections

Sand dredges at work in the Mekong River. - Post Staff PHNOM PENH: Prime Minister Hun Manet has ordered the temporary suspension of sand dredging at locations where riverbank collapses are occurring until officials and technical experts are able to determine the cause of the erosion. The directive was issued during the 25th plenary session of the Council of Ministers on Aug 28, amid growing public concern and social media allegations linking riverbank erosion to sand dredging operations. Manet instructed the Sand Resources Management Committee, capital and provincial administrations and relevant departments to immediately inspect affected sites and determine whether the erosion was caused by dredging, strong currents, natural changes or other factors. “For any location where the riverbank is collapsing and sand dredging is taking place, suspend the dredging first. Do not make the matter complicated,” he said. “If we need two weeks to conduct an assessment, but the bank continues to collapse while dredging also continues there, the issues will become entangled,” he added. The prime minister stressed that the suspension was a precautionary measure while technical findings remained inconclusive, rather than a predetermined judgment that sand dredging was responsible for every case of riverbank erosion. “If the cause is not yet clear, suspend the operation first. If a riverbank is collapsing at a site where dredging is taking place, halt the activity and conduct a thorough assessment,” he said. Under the directive, provincial departments responsible for water resources, the environment, and mines and energy must jointly inspect conditions at affected sites, with coordination from the Sand Resources Management Committee and capital or provincial administrations. If subnational officials lack the expertise, equipment or technical capacity to complete an assessment, local authorities should immediately seek assistance from the relevant national ministries and institutions. Manet said the physical presence of officials at affected locations was essential. Authorities should not leave an information vacuum or delay their response, as this could heighten public anxiety and allow unverified claims to spread. “In some places, the riverbank is collapsing because the water level is rising quickly and the current is strong. In other places, it may be the natural impact of the current; we still need to investigate,” he said. After the investigations and assessments are completed, the Sand Resources Management Committee and local administrations must promptly release the findings, clarify the causes and inform affected communities of the proposed solutions. Manet noted that riverbank erosion had occurred both in areas with dredging operations and in places where no such activity was taking place. He therefore urged technical institutions to communicate with the public based on evidence and professional assessments, rather than issuing blanket denials or general conclusions. The directive followed discussions between the prime minister and Minister of Mines and Energy Keo Rottanak, who had briefed him on riverbank erosion cases and their possible relationship with sand dredging. Alongside his demand for swift official action, Manet advised officials to choose their words carefully when explaining technical issues to the public. Individual phrases could be removed from their original context and used for ridicule on social media, obscuring the intended technical message, he warned. He referred to online mockery of remarks attributed to a government official about sand and rock, saying such episodes demonstrated why officials needed to speak precisely and focus directly on the issue under discussion. The prime minister also called for action against false information, alleging that some social media users had combined images of a collapsed riverbank at one location with photographs of sand-dredging vessels taken elsewhere to create the impression of a direct connection. However, he indicated that countering misinformation must go hand in hand with field inspections, the disclosure of evidence and clear explanations to residents about the measures authorities intend to take to address erosion and prevent further risks. The Ministry of Water Resources and Meteorology has previously conducted outreach in several provinces on the legal framework, management mechanisms and technical standards governing sand businesses. At a June 12 meeting in Koh Kong province, ministry and provincial officials discussed responsible sand operations, their potential effects on residents’ livelihoods and the need to safeguard riverbanks. The ministry and Stung Treng provincial authorities have also sought to strengthen the management of sand operations, focusing on environmental sustainability, the prevention of riverbank erosion and the reduction of negative effects on water currents. Manet’s directive does not impose a nationwide suspension of sand dredging. It applies specifically to locations where riverbanks are actively collapsing and dredging is taking place nearby, allowing technical assessments to be conducted while reducing the risk of further damage. - The Phnom Penh Post/ANN Follow us on our official WhatsApp channel for breaking news alerts and key updates! PH says high-profile corruption convicts should serve full sentences as Najib pardon bid looms

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 9): Pakatan Harapan (PH) has stressed that those convicted of corruption or abuse of power, particularly in high-profile cases, should serve the full sentences imposed by the courts. Any decision involving high-profile cases must take into account public confidence in the country’s commitment to its reform and anti-corruption agenda, the ruling coalition said in a statement issued Wednesday midnight. The principle of the rule of law also requires that ongoing judicial proceedings be allowed to conclude in an orderly and independent manner, without creating the perception that other considerations have pre-empted the process, PH said. While the statement did not name any individual, it comes amid reports that the Pardons Board, chaired by Malaysia’s King Sultan Ibrahim, is scheduled to meet on Sept 11 to consider, among other matters, imprisoned former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s bid for a pardon over his convictions linked to the multibillion-ringgit 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) scandal. Chinese-language daily Sin Chew Daily reported that Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh, who sits on the Pardons Board by virtue of her ministerial post, briefed the PH presidential council on Tuesday night. The three component parties of PH, including Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s Parti Keadilan Rakyat, have reportedly reiterated their opposition to a pardon for Najib, according to the report. Najib has been imprisoned since Aug 23, 2022, after the Federal Court dismissed his final appeal in the RM42 million SRC International Sdn Bhd case. He was sentenced to 12 years in jail and fined RM210 million. Najib has consistently maintained his innocence and subsequently sought a royal pardon. The Pardons Board, chaired by the 16th Yang di-Pertuan Agong Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, reduced his prison term to six years and the fine to RM50 million in 2024, before the King’s five-year reign ended. Najib also sought to compel the government to enforce an alleged addendum order issued by Al-Sultan Abdullah allowing him to serve the remainder of his reduced sentence under house arrest. The application, however, was dismissed by the court last year. Najib was separately found guilty in December 2025 on four charges of abuse of power and 21 money-laundering charges involving more than RM2 billion in funds linked to 1MDB. He was sentenced to 15 years in prison and ordered to pay a RM11.38 billion fine. He is appealing the conviction. All eyes on UMNO assembly The PH statement also comes as Najib’s party Umno is set to convene its annual general assembly from Sept 9 to 12. Umno, the lynchpin of Barisan Nasional (BN), is part of the Anwar-led multi-party ruling government and has previously been vocal in its push to secure house arrest for Najib. Umno leaders have yet to respond to Najib’s alleged fresh bid for a pardon, although the issue is expected to be among those debated by delegates at the assembly.

US to ban Canadian motorcycle, dairy, alcohol imports as trade war sizzles
['Gram Slattery, Promit Mukherjee & Ryan Patrick Jones']

WASHINGTON (Sept 8): The United States banned a broad swath of Canadian alcoholic beverages, motorcycles and dairy products from import on Tuesday, sharply escalating an already acrimonious trade spat. The import bans, which go into effect on Sept 29 and were published on the White House's website, came after Canada's own retaliatory tariffs on US goods took effect after midnight on Tuesday. Those Canadian levies themselves followed 50% tariffs that the United States imposed on some US$20 billion of Canadian goods last month, after several rounds of negotiations collapsed. The breakdown has widened a rift between the longtime allies, who have blamed each other for the failed talks, spurred Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to urge a further shift away from Canada's biggest trading partner, and cast doubt on the viability of the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement. "We have everything we need to pivot and prosper," Carney said on Tuesday in a video posted on YouTube. "That pivot will come at a cost. There's always a cost to action. But it doesn't come close to the cost of standing still," he said. The U.S. bans appeared to cover most alcohol products, including beer and various types of wine, whisky, bourbon, rum, vodka, vermouth, tequila, mezcal, and brandy. The dairy ban covers whey protein, invert molasses, cane molasses and non-alcoholic beer, per notices on the White House's website. In addition to the import bans, various cheese products were added to a list of products subject to a 50% tariff, but not banned outright. Some paper, aluminum, wood, furniture, lighting and other products were also added to the list. A US official said President Donald Trump's pre-existing threat to increase tariffs on Canadian autos from 25% to 50% on Jan 1 remained in effect. The official added that US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer had spoken with Dominic LeBlanc, Canada's minister responsible for bilateral US trade, over the past couple of days, and the pair were expected to speak again in the coming days to see if there was an alternative path for the two countries. In a social media post on Tuesday night, LeBlanc criticised the latest US measures and said he was in contact with Greer regarding a path forward. "As has been the case for the last 18 months, our first priority remains on protecting and supporting Canadian workers, farmers, families, and businesses from these unjustified actions," he wrote. Ottawa strikes back Ottawa's retaliatory measures, which in turn provoked Washington's move on Tuesday night, were designed to put economic and political pressure on Washington, Canadian government officials said. Those counter-tariffs cover some US$20 billion of US goods, with duties ranging from 15% to 50% across products from steel and furniture to clothing and electronics, and are expected to hit sectors in some competitive states such as Michigan and Ohio, ahead of US midterm elections in November. While the tariffs affect a small amount of exports compared with total trade between the US and Canada, some analysts worry the standoff could destabilise the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement, the free-trade pact that succeeded Nafta. Together they have underpinned commerce across North America for decades. "What we are worried about is an escalatory spiral," said Michael Harvey, executive director of the Canadian Agri-Food Trade Alliance and a member of Carney's advisory committee on bilateral US economic relations. "But at the same time, we totally understand that the prime minister needs to find areas of leverage." Trump has been lobbing various attacks at Canada on Truth Social in recent days. On Monday, he said Canadian private jet maker Bombardier would no longer be allowed to sell its planes in the United States unless it started manufacturing in the country. He also shared a map of North America draped in the US flag, including Canada and Mexico, and an AI-generated image reviving a running jab at Carney, calling him "Governor," a reference to his repeated taunt that Canada should become the 51st US state. On Tuesday, hours before the latest import bans, Trump directed the General Services Administration, a US government body responsible for providing services for the federal government, to coordinate with the US Trade Representative and "REMOVE Canadian-origin products from GSA’s Multiple Award Schedules unless Canada restores full and fair reciprocity for American Farmers and Companies." Various sectors hit Trump's tariffs implemented last month hit sectors including wine, furniture, dairy products, cement, clothing, fishing rods and hockey equipment, covering US$20 billion, or 5%, of Canadian exports to the US. A Sapporo spokesperson said the brewer is considering moving a limited amount of production of non-alcoholic drinks from Canada to the US due to tariff risks, but no final decision has been made. Sapporo owns Ontario-based Sleeman Breweries. Canada accounts for more than half of the Japanese firm's overseas beer sales. According to Canadian and US government data, Canada has shipped almost 68% of total exports to the US this year, out of which roughly 80% moved duty-free due to exemptions under the USMCA pact. Protections under the agreement have provided the domestic economy some resilience. Last month's tariffs, imposed under a Depression-era US law, do not allow Ottawa to exercise USMCA exemptions. Concerns about the USMCA's future have fuelled uncertainty about investment and growth, as Canada wages a trade war against an economy 13 times its size. Polls also show Carney has broad support from Canadians, but that could disappear within months as the consequences of the trade war sink in, according to political analysts. A new poll from Angus Reid on Tuesday showed that approval of Carney's performance jumped 11 points to 62% from an August poll. Meanwhile, just 20% of Americans approved of Trump's tariffs on Canadian goods, a Reuters/Ipsos poll found. Trump threatened last month to raise US tariffs on all cars, trucks and automotive parts from Canada to 50% starting Jan 1, and signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario as Lake America. Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong’s first Chinese leader, dies at 89

(Sept 9): Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong’s first leader after Britain handed the city back to China in 1997, has died. He was 89. Tung “passed away peacefully in the presence of his beloved family members” on Tuesday local time, according to a statement from his office. “Mr Tung dedicated his life with an unwavering commitment to the service” of China and Hong Kong, it added. Tung took office on July 1, 1997, hours after the Chinese flag rose on the UK’s last major colony, concluding a century and a half of colonial rule. “The eyes of the world are on us as Hong Kong accepts the great honor, and the challenge, of charting new waters, which will make history,” he said in his inaugural speech. “We are confident that we will rise to the challenge and build a brighter and better future.” The Shanghai-born Tung was Hong Kong’s first leader under the “one country, two systems” arrangement. The policy was intended to guarantee that the former British colony would keep, for at least 50 years, its capitalist system as well as personal freedoms not enjoyed by mainland Chinese. His admission that China had helped bail out his family’s shipping empire in the 1980s raised concern among some business leaders about his willingness to act independently of Beijing. Those suspicions were an early taste of the tensions that would linger for decades between China and the semi-autonomous Chinese city. Tung’s time as chief executive, as the city’s leader is called, was plagued by a succession of crises, including some of the biggest pro-democracy demonstrations on Chinese soil since the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown and the 2003 SARS epidemic. An estimated 500,000 people took part in a 2003 protest of his administration’s attempt to introduce a national security law that threatened to curb the city’s cherished freedoms. That law was finally passed in 2024 after officials purged pro-democracy lawmakers from the local legislature. Housing program Tung’s plan to build 85,000 housing flats each year to meet demand coincided with the Asian financial crisis, and he was blamed for crashing the home market. Decades later, the merits of his proposal remain the subject of debate, as Hong Kong homes are ranked the least affordable in the world. His own housing was a matter of interest as well. He elected not to live in the Government House, the chief executive’s official residence, after expressing concern over the Art Deco-styled mansion’s “bad feng shui.” Instead, he continued to live in his own home. His neighbor, a Goldman Sachs investment banker, moved to make way for the government to rent the adjoining apartment to create more space for Tung, who eventually bought the 3,335-square-feet flat in 2021 for HK$160 million (US$20.6 million or RM82.99 million), according to property records. His popularity ratings slumped at home and in Beijing, with then-President Hu Jintao in December 2004 telling the Hong Kong leader to do better. Tung, who was said to work an 18-hour day, resigned in 2005 halfway through his second term, citing his declining health and age. He was 67 at the time. That year, he was appointed to China’s top advisory body, the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference. In 2014, he founded the Our Hong Kong Foundation, a think tank that counts numerous tycoons among its members. Its stated mission is to “contribute to Hong Kong’s prosperity and stability as well as its sustainable development under the ‘One Country, Two Systems’ principle.” His death raises immediate questions about how and where he’ll be officially commemorated, and whether President Xi Jinping will attend any memorial events. There is no precedent for that, since Tung is the first former leader of a Chinese special administrative region to die. Two birthdays Tung was born in Shanghai on July 7, 1937. On the lunar calender traditionally used to mark holidays and seasons in China, that was the 29th day of the fifth month — which is why, when the family moved to Hong Kong before Tung had entered his teens, his birthday was given to authorities as May 29. He never corrected the record, and that date remained part of his official biography. “It’s good to have two birthdays,” he said in 1997, according to the Post . He was the first of four children of shipping magnate Tung Chao Yung, founder of what today is Orient Overseas Container Line, and his wife, Koo Lee Ching. After completing secondary school in Hong Kong, Tung studied in the UK, graduating in 1960 from the University of Liverpool with a degree in marine engineering. He spent nine years working in the US, including at General Electric Co, according to his biography. His time in both places deepened his interest in sports including soccer and basketball. He was known especially as a diehard fan of Liverpool Football Club. The Hong Kong government’s 2003 yearbook includes a photo of him holding up a team jersey at a practice session when Liverpool visited for a friendly with a Hong Kong team. Tung took over the family business after his father died in 1982. The company soon hit financial troubles and needed a US$120 million rescue package that was arranged by Henry Fok, one of Hong Kong’s most prominent pro-China businessmen. It was during his candidacy to lead Hong Kong that Tung acknowledged that some of that money had come from mainland Chinese funds. Fok, as a vice chairman of the Chinese parliament’s main consultative body starting in 1993, was reported to have introduced Tung to then-Chinese President Jiang Zemin, according to Reuters ’ obituary of Fok. That introduction paved the way for Tung to become China’s preferred candidate to lead Hong Kong. In the December 1996 election to decide the first chief executive, a 400-person selection committee named by China’s government voted overwhelmingly for Tung. Tung was married to Betty Chiu Hung Ping and had three children. Uploaded by Isabelle Francis

Air traffic control issue disrupts flights at major UK airports

LONDON (Sept 8): Flights at major British airports were disrupted on Tuesday by a technical fault at air traffic control provider NATS, the latest in a series of failures that renewed questions about the resilience of Britain's aviation infrastructure. The cancellation of more than 1,000 flights and delays to hundreds more renew scrutiny of NATS three years after a flight-plan processing failure caused even more widespread disruption. As passengers waited for information in departure halls across the country on Tuesday, airlines questioned whether the country's air traffic control system was fit for purpose. NATS said at 1834 GMT that the issue, which had impacted its flight data processing system, had been resolved. It had earlier said that "safety was not compromised." "Recovery from today’s system issue has taken longer than we had hoped. Our system issue is now resolved, we are operating normally and working as hard as possible to clear the backlog of flights," NATS said on X. The traffic control provider later said in an update on X that it would take time to recover from the disruption, adding that "this has been a very complex recovery and has created difficulties for the whole aviation network". CEO Martin Rolfe told Sky News that NATS had not "fully done the investigation" to find the reason behind the technical issue that caused the disruption. "We don't have an idea yet of exactly what went wrong," Rolfe said. Flights delayed and cancelled According to data from flight-tracking website Flightradar24, 1,300 flights to and from UK airports were cancelled on Tuesday. Another 177 flights had been cancelled for Wednesday, nearly all of them at Heathrow, the country's largest airport, it added. Heathrow said at 2019 GMT that arrivals to the airport had been suspended for the remainder of Tuesday, and while departures had resumed, the disruption was expected to continue. Earlier, data on flight-tracking platform FlightAware said some 490 departures were delayed at six airports, including Heathrow, Gatwick, London City, Luton, Edinburgh and Bristol as of 1518 GMT. Some 525 arrivals at those six airports were either cancelled or delayed, the website data showed. At Heathrow, 38 of 661 scheduled arrivals had been cancelled or were unable to operate, according to aviation analytics company Cirium. British Airways was the most affected carrier at the airport, cancelling 16 of 333 scheduled departures. "The severity of the issue means there will be a significant knock-on impact for customers and colleagues," British Airways said in a statement. Europe's traffic-filled skies Air traffic control is a tightly timed system in Europe's extremely busy skies. Aviation analyst John Strickland said the consequences of even a relatively short outage can be severe because delays quickly cascade through tightly scheduled airline networks. "A few hours of outage may on the face of it sound limited but the impact is enormous when a substantial number of airports across the UK are affected," Strickland said. Ryanair said around 150,000 of its passengers had been affected by delays of up to eight hours and that it had cancelled more than 200 flights, and called on NATS chief executive Martin Rolfe to resign. "How many more failures do passengers have to suffer before overpaid failure NATS CEO, Martin Rolfe, accepts responsibility for his repeated mismanagement and resigns?" Ryanair chief operating officer Neal McMahon said. NATS did not immediately respond to a request for comment on McMahon's statement. Wizz Air also called for urgent reform of the air traffic control provider, saying airlines, passengers and airports should not continue to bear the consequences of recurring system failures. "A critical national infrastructure provider should not repeatedly bring the aviation system to a standstill. NATS is simply not fit for purpose in its current form," Wizz Air said. Britain's aviation regulator said it would expect NATS to share a full report of Tuesday's incident. The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) said it would then consider whether any further steps need to be taken to secure the reliability of the UK's air traffic control system. In 2024, the CAA said NATS needed to review its contingency plans for outages after the automatic processing of flight plans had malfunctioned a year earlier, causing chaos across Britain's airports. Airline bosses said that outage had cost them over £100 million (US$135.49 million) in refunds and compensation. In July last year, a radar-related technical issue in Britain's air traffic control system disrupted flights for over four hours at major airports in London and elsewhere, including Heathrow. CLICK LINK By Maizatul Jamny Muhammad Rosli and Nazira Hasanah Nasaruddin BAGAN SERAI : At just one year old, Orked knows nothing of extinction, shrinking populations or the responsibility her tiny generation may one day carry. The youngest resident of Bukit Merah Orang Utan Island is one of 15 orangutans whose future could become far more significant than simply growing up within the sanctuary. For the Bukit Merah Orang Utan Island Foundation, Orked and those who come after her could eventually form part of a 50-strong “assurance population”, large enough to offer hope of repopulating the wild should catastrophe one day devastate orangutans in their natural habitat. The foundation’s adviser, Azmil Khuzaid Zakaria, said the long-term plan, which could take between 15 and 20 years to achieve, is rooted in a sobering possibility that a severe collapse in the wild could one day make a protected population such as Bukit Merah’s crucial to rebuilding numbers. “The 50 orangutans are to essentially maintain that assurance population, meaning if there is any massive failure in the wild, this is enough to start repopulating (the wild). Of course, it will take decades,” he told Bernama during a media familiarisation trip at Bukit Merah Laketown Resort here on Sunday. The foundation’s updated 2026 list shows its present residents comprise eight males and seven females, ranging from Orked, aged one, and two-year-old Aggy to long-time residents such as B.J., 40, Baboon, 39, and Ah Ling, 32. A BIOLOGICAL SAFETY NET Azmil Khuzaid said conservation efforts over the years appeared to have slowed the decline of orangutans, but the situation remained fragile and the foundation was not yet prepared to pursue its earlier ambition of releasing animals from the island into the wild. He said the original plan was to gradually return orangutans to the wild as the island population grew rather than continuously expanding the facility, but this has been put on hold as long-term captive animals require training before release, coupled with the still uncertain state of wild populations. That decision ultimately gave rise to a different idea. Instead of viewing the island merely as a temporary home, the foundation would expand it sufficiently to maintain a larger population capable of acting as a biological safety net. Currently, Azmil Khuzaid said slightly less than five acres of the 15-acre island are being used, and the existing area is almost at capacity with room for only another two or three orangutans, or perhaps five if stretched. He said an additional five acres, consisting largely of spaces for the animals rather than administrative facilities, could accommodate about 60 orangutans, although the foundation intends to keep the population at around 50. SPACE, DOMINANCE AND THE GENE POOL Space is not simply a matter of numbers. With eight of the present 15 orangutans being male, the foundation also has to contend with the animals’ natural drive for dominance as they mature, requiring some males to be kept apart. Azmil Khuzaid recalled how Mike, the island’s original dominant male, fought with B.J. in an encounter that showed just how serious such conflicts could become. “So, he (Mike) got into a fight with B.J., and he lost. But we have separated them (after that). However, Mike didn’t live much longer after that,” he added. The need to separate different Bornean orangutan subspecies further complicates the equation, while at the same time the foundation must also manage the genetic diversity of what remains a relatively closed population. To broaden the gene pool and reduce the risk of inbreeding over successive generations, Azmil Khuzaid said the foundation is working with zoos and exploring cooperation with other organisations housing orangutans through animal exchanges. One of its orangutans is presently at Melaka Zoo following an attempt to breed it with a female there. As the pairing did not work out, he said the foundation plans to bring the animal back and send a pair in exchange, while discussions are also under way with several other organisations. He said growing the population naturally is itself a test of patience, as an orangutan infant typically remains with its mother until five to seven years of age and the mother would normally not become pregnant again during that period. “So, if we solely rely on that sort of organic growth, it’ll take too long. So, we are looking at other options of bringing in orangutans from other places as well,” he said. Beyond preservation, he hopes a population of that size could also give researchers greater opportunities to understand orangutan social structures and behaviours, which are difficult to observe in the wild. He said an orangutan can remain so elusive in its natural habitat that researchers may spend days searching without encountering one, making the island population potentially valuable in building scientific knowledge about the species. THE COST OF KEEPING HOPE ALIVE Yet keeping that safety net alive comes at a substantial price. Azmil Khuzaid said the foundation historically depended heavily on funding from EMKAY Group founder, the late Tan Sri Mustapha Kamal Abu Bakar, who pioneered the establishment of Bukit Merah Orang Utan Island, while visitor ticket sales now cover a significant part of the island’s expenses. Since joining the foundation in 2020, however, he said it had become increasingly clear that orangutan conservation should not rest on the shoulders of one individual or organisation. He said the foundation has since worked with organisations, including the Malaysian Palm Oil Green Conservation Foundation and most recently, Marriott Bonvoy, while continuing to seek other like-minded partners. “It’s up to all of us to play our parts. It’s not just about the money,” he said, adding that organisations could also contribute their time, expertise or other resources. The challenge will grow as the population does, with Azmil Khuzaid estimating that tripling the number of orangutans would also triple operating costs. Energy alone already accounts for nearly a third of operating expenses. A diesel generator powers the island, and in recent years electricity has been available for only about 12 hours daily, while a planned shift to partial solar power is expected to meet about 30 per cent of its energy requirements. Restoring round-the-clock power, he said, would allow food to be stored on the island and provide greater support during emergencies. Azmil Khuzaid said behind the animals are also 17 people, including rangers, nurses and a veterinarian, responsible for keeping the island running and its residents cared for. A SHARED RESPONSIBILITY Meanwhile, the foundation is considering reviving its individual volunteer programme, which has not restarted since the COVID-19 pandemic. Before then, “voluntourism” programmes drew people from abroad and locally to spend weeks helping with work on the island. “They (tourists) would come here, spend a few weeks and do volunteer work. They paid travel agents for the joy of cleaning the orangutan cages. So, it’s an interesting concept but Alhamdulillah, there are people out there in the world who want to do this,” he added. For now, reaching 50 orangutans at Bukit Merah Orang Utan Island remains a vision measured not in months or even a few years, but in decades. One that will require new enclosures, greater financial resources, careful genetic management and more partners willing to share the responsibility. BENGALURU (Sept 8): Qualcomm on Tuesday reached a deal to develop custom chips with Amazon for artificial intelligence (AI) data centres, giving it the right to acquire about US$4 billion (RM16.2 billion) in shares in exchange for US$60 billion in business with the chipmaker. As part of the deal, Qualcomm has granted Amazon a warrant that could allow it to acquire up to US$4 billion of its shares over the next decade. The warrant is tied to the companies' striking business agreements over the period. Shares of San Diego, California-based Qualcomm rose more than 7% in early trading on Tuesday. The stock has slipped about 1% this year, through last close, as a rebound in August only partly recouped steep losses sparked by weaker smartphone demand. The warrant lets Amazon buy Qualcomm shares at a fixed price of US$161.26 apiece, according to a regulatory filing. Such arrangements are becoming more common across the AI supply chain, raising questions among some investors about increasingly intertwined financial relationships as chipmakers offer equity incentives tied to future orders. The agreement is the latest sign Qualcomm's efforts to expand beyond its core smartphone business are gaining traction, as it faces the eventual loss of its modem business from Apple. Qualcomm has spent the past year pitching custom chips and other data-centre technology to cloud providers seeking alternatives to Nvidia's dominant AI processors, with Amazon now joining a growing roster of customers that are backing its pivot. The partnership comes weeks after Marvell Technology struck a similar custom AI chip deal with Alphabet's Google, giving the tech giant the right to buy a stake worth up to US$12.2 billion. Under Tuesday's deal, Qualcomm and Amazon will work together on chips for AI inference, a fast-growing market focused on running trained AI models that has become a key battleground among semiconductor firms. The companies will also develop high-speed optical connectivity technologies, including solutions extending to 1.6 terabits per second, to support growing bandwidth demands in AI data centres. As part of the tie-up, Qualcomm plans to expand its use of Amazon Web Services and infrastructure for chip design workloads, aiming to shorten development cycles. In June, Qualcomm said it had signed on Microsoft and Meta as customers for its new data-centre chips and expects revenue from two custom-chip hyperscale customers before year end. Pesanan Tun Abdul Razak tentang rasuah ancam negara masih relevan – Anwar

KUALA LUMPUR – Ancaman korupsi atau rasuah pernah dikenal pasti sebagai salah satu daripada tiga cabaran utama negara oleh Perdana Menteri Kedua, Allahyarham Tun Abdul Razak Hussein sekitar era 1970-an masih relevan sehingga kini. Perdana Menteri, Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim berkata, tiga ancaman yang dikenali sebagai ‘3C’ itu merangkumi komunisme (communism), idealogi atau pegangan politik (communalism) dan korupsi (corruption). Menurut beliau, meskipun ancaman komunisme bersenjata seperti yang dihadapi negara pada ketika itu sudah tidak lagi berlaku, namun ancaman berkaitan fahaman asing, sentimen perkauman dan rasuah masih perlu diberi perhatian. “Yang ketiga, bayangkan tahun 70-an, Tun Abdul Razak menyebut ancaman ketiga yang bahaya bagi negara (ialah) corruption (korupsi). Itu ‘3C’,” katanya ketika berucap pada Program Mengenai Negarawan Tun Abdul Razak “Arkitek Pembangunan Negara Bangsa” di sini, hari ini. Anwar berkata, Tun Abdul Razak ketika itu turut mengingatkan golongan muda supaya tidak menganggap rasuah sebagai sesuatu yang jauh daripada kehidupan mereka. Katanya, Bapa Pembangunan itu memahami bahawa anak muda pada ketika itu lantang menentang rasuah kerana mereka belum berdepan dengan kedudukan atau kuasa yang membuka ruang kepada amalan berkenaan. “Ya lah, kamu semua sekarang anak muda menentang rasuah. Menolak dengan keras sebab tak ada orang nak rasuah kamu. “Tapi sebaik jadi nanti, (ada jawatan), masa itu dah mula kendur (goyah),” katanya ketika mengimbas kembali pesanan Allahyarham. Anwar berkata, pesanan tersebut kemudiannya dibawa oleh beberapa penceramah ke universiti-universiti bagi memberi kesedaran kepada golongan mahasiswa mengenai bahaya rasuah. Beliau menyifatkan perkara itu sebagai antara pesanan Allahyarham yang mampu merentasi zaman dan kekal mempunyai kaitan dengan cabaran negara pada masa kini. “Communalism (komunisme) masih tebal. Dan corruption (korupsi) masih menjadi salah satu masalah besar,” tegasnya. Beliau menambah, generasi muda khususnya perlu memahami bahawa perjuangan membina negara bukan sekadar mengenai pencapaian sejarah, sebaliknya memerlukan penghayatan gagasan serta penerimaan terhadap pesanan tokoh terdahulu. – KOSMO! Pempengaruh maut selepas suntik besarkan alat sulit
Hib Glam, Hiburan, Rencam, Selebriti Dunia, Terkini

PETALING JAYA – Hasrat seorang ahli perniagaan juga pempengaruh British-Nigeria, Igho ‘Tiny’ Ubiribo untuk membesarkan alat sulit bertukar tragedi apabila dia meninggal dunia selepas menjalani prosedur suntikan pengisi zakar di Bangkok, Thailand. Lelaki berusia 43, menghembuskan nafas terakhir pada awal pagi 6 Mac lalu, sehari selepas menjalani prosedur kosmetik berkenaan di sebuah klinik yang tidak dinamakan di Bangkok. Menurut laporan Guardian Nigeria yang memetik prosiding inkues di Inner West London Coroners’ Court, kelmarin, kira-kira 40 mililiter (ml) campuran asid hyaluronik dan lidocaine disuntik pada zakarnya bagi meningkatkan ukuran lilit alat sulit. Ubiribo dilaporkan menjalani prosedur itu pada 5 Mac sebelum dia dan isterinya, Danielle Simba Allen, ke sebuah hotel di Bangkok dan mendapatkan urutan. Bagaimanapun, ketika urutan, dia mengadu sakit dada sebelum pengsan sebanyak dua kali sebelum dikejarkan dengan ambulans ke Hospital Sukhumvit. Pada awalnya dia masih sedar serta mampu menjawab soalan doktor namun kesihatannya merosot apabila dia sekali lagi tidak sedarkan diri sebelum imbasan tomografi berkomputer (CT) sempat dilakukan. Doktor kemudian mengesahkan dia mengalami embolisme pulmonari iaitu satu atau lebih saluran darah (arteri) di dalam paru-paru tersumbat dan memindahkannya ke unit rawatan rapi (ICU). Panas, jerebu, aktiviti lasak jadi ‘perangkap maut’

PETALING JAYA – Gabungan cuaca panas, jerebu dan aktiviti fizikal lasak boleh menjadi ‘pe­rangkap maut’ apabila tubuh dipaksa menghasilkan dan menanggung haba pada kadar yang melebihi kemampuan untuk menyejukkannya. Lebih membimbangkan, kea­daan itu boleh berlaku kepada individu muda dan cergas yang merasakan tubuh mereka masih mampu bertahan, sedangkan fungsi otak mungkin sudah mula terjejas sehingga menjejaskan keupayaan membuat keputusan untuk berhenti. Pakar Perubatan Kesihatan Awam Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia, Prof. Madya Dr. Mohd. Dzulkhairi Mohd. Rani berkata, apabila suhu teras badan me­ningkat secara melampau, haba boleh menyebabkan kerosakan kepada sel dan protein selain mencetuskan keradangan, gangguan peredaran darah serta ketidakseimbangan elektrolit. Ujarnya, gabungan pro­ses itu menyebabkan fungsi otak terganggu sehingga seseorang boleh mengalami perubahan tingkah laku, kekeliruan dan hilang koordinasi sebelum menjadi lebih serius se­perti sawan, tidak sedarkan diri, koma serta kerosakan pelbagai organ. Katanya, strok haba boleh berlaku dengan cepat apabila aktiviti fizikal lasak dilakukan dalam keadaan suhu persekitaran tinggi dan kelembapan yang mengurangkan keupayaan tubuh membuang haba, ditambah keletihan serta kehilangan cecair dan elektrolit. “Pada satu tahap, mekanisme kawalan badan gagal dan kea­daan boleh berubah daripada keletihan kepada strok haba serta kegagalan organ dalam tempoh yang singkat,” katanya ketika dihubungi Kosmo! semalam Beliau berkata, keadaan menjadi lebih berisiko apabila jerebu berlaku serentak kerana haba meningkatkan tekanan terhadap sistem kardiovaskular, manakala jerebu pula menambah tekanan terhadap sistem pernafasan dan kardiovaskular. “Semasa aktiviti lasak, tubuh menghasilkan lebih banyak haba dan individu akan bernafas lebih cepat serta lebih dalam, sekali gus meningkatkan jumlah bahan pencemar yang disedut. “Gabungan haba, jerebu dan aktiviti lasak boleh meningkatkan tekanan fisiologi keseluruhan serta mengurangkan keupayaan tubuh menyesuaikan diri dengan persekitaran,” katanya. Semalam Kosmo! melaporkan, seorang pelajar Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) maut, manakala lapan lagi rebah ketika Program Komander Kesatria Endurance Challenge UiTM Se-Malaysia 2026 di Kampus UiTM Jengka, Jumaat lalu. Sementara itu, Pensyarah Perubatan Biokimia, Jabatan Biokimia Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, Dr. Nuraqilah Mohd. Murshid berkata, strok haba akibat aktiviti fizikal boleh berlaku apabila otot menghasilkan haba jauh lebih cepat daripada kemampuan badan membuangnya. “Ketika senaman berat, penghasilan haba boleh meningkat antara 15 hingga 20 kali ganda berbanding ketika berehat, manakala kelembapan tinggi pula menghalang penyejatan peluh yang merupakan mekanisme utama badan untuk menyejukkan diri. “Strok haba eksersional bukan penyakit orang yang lemah. ­Mangsanya selalunya individu muda, cergas dan bersemangat tinggi seperti atlet, rekrut tentera dan peserta program ketahanan. “Kecergasan bukan perisai. Ia hanya membolehkan seseorang terus bergerak lebih lama sebelum badannya akhirnya mengalah,” jelasnya. Beliau berkata, risiko lebih banyak ditentukan keadaan badan pada hari kejadian termasuk dehidrasi, kurang tidur, tidak cukup tempoh aklimatisasi terhadap haba, demam atau jangkitan, pemakaian atau kelengkapan tebal serta penggunaan suplemen berstimulan. “Antara perkara paling kritikal ialah mangsa mungkin gagal menyedari tanda awal kerana hipertermia boleh menjejaskan otak yang sepatutnya menentukan keputusan untuk berhenti. “Antara tanda awal boleh diperhatikan adalah perubahan tingkah laku dan kekeliruan. Jawapan yang tidak munasabah atau percakapan pelat, cepat marah, bertindak luar tabiat, langkah goyah, senget atau tersasar dari laluan serta alami sakit kepala, pening dan loya. “Dalam strok haba eksersio­nal, kulit mangsa selalunya masih berpeluh. Menunggu kulit menjadi kering sebelum bertindak merupakan kesilapan yang boleh meragut nyawa,” katanya. Tambahnya, apabila jerebu turut berlaku, peningkatan kadar pernafasan ketika bersenam menyebabkan individu menyedut lebih banyak bahan pencemar seperti zarah halus PM2.5 jauh ke dalam saluran pernafasan.

BCCK Named Official Venue For National-level Malaysia Day 2026 Celebrations

KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 (Bernama) -- The Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) in Sarawak has been officially named the venue for the national-level Malaysia Day celebrations on Sept 16. The decision to hold the main celebration indoors was made to provide a climate-controlled and safe environment for dignitaries and cultural troupes, in view of the current haze affecting parts of Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia. Information Department (JAPEN) Cyber Media Division assistant director Yumna Baharuddin said Sarawak’s selection as host aligns with the 2020 Cabinet decision to implement a rotational system between Sarawak, Sabah and Peninsular Malaysia. “This rotational system ensures that every Malaysian, regardless of geographic location, shares directly in the spirit and historical resonance of Malaysia Day. "Following Penang’s hosting in 2025, bringing the celebrations back to Sarawak underscores the Federal Government's unwavering commitment to strengthening national integration across all regions,” she said during an exclusive interview on TRAXX FM today. Elaborating on the significance of the date, Yumna emphasised the distinct historical significance of the two national observances. “While Aug 31 commemorates the independence of the Federation of Malaya in 1957, Sept 16 marks the 1963 historic unification of Malaya, Sabah, Sarawak and Singapore into a single sovereign federation,” she said. This year's celebration retains the theme “Malaysia MADANI: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati” (Prosperity Enjoyed Together), paired with Sarawak’s unity tagline “Segulai Sejalai” (Walking Hand-in-Hand). The main ceremonial event at BCCK will feature an array of symbolic and cultural performances, including an inter-ethnic welcoming segment blending silat, hadra, gendang pampat and lion dance performances. It will also include the signing of the Malaysia Proclamation Book by national and state leaders. The historical volume was transported under the custody of the Sabah State Archives, pursuant to the Sabah State Records and Archives Enactment 2007. Other highlights include the ceremonial cutting of pulut kuning and a tri-state artiste showcase featuring prominent performers Dayang Nurfaizah, Faizal Tahir and Stacy. JAPEN and its partner agencies have also arranged a series of satellite events from Sept 10 to 16. Liverpool announce five-year sponsorship deal with Turkish Airlines

(Sept 8): Liverpool have agreed a five-year deal for Turkish Airlines to become their main club partner from June 1, 2027, which means the first change in the Anfield side's leading shirt sponsor since 2010, ending a 17-year run for Standard Chartered. The deal announced on Tuesday will be worth in excess of £300 million (US$405.78 million or RM1.6 billion) according to media reports, which would place it among the most lucrative in the Premier League. "Turkish Airlines is a globally recognised organisation with an extensive international network and we look forward to beginning our partnership and building a strong relationship together, with already strong foundations built from those special memories back in 2005," he added, referring to Liverpool's Champions League final comeback win in Istanbul. The deal adds to a growing sponsorship portfolio within football for Turkish Airlines, who are an official partner of the Champions League and main sponsor of Türkiye's national team. JAKARTA (Sept 8): Nearly 900 hectares of forest and land fire remained unextinguished across six priority provinces in Indonesia as of Tuesday despite weeks of intense ground and aerial firefighting operations. The National Disaster Mitigation Agency's disaster data, information and communication centre acting head Berton Panjaitan said almost 1,500 hectares had burned across West, Central and South Kalimantan, as well as Riau, Jambi and South Sumatra, with more than 550 hectares reported extinguished so far. He said more than 40,000 personnel were deployed for ground firefighting while aerial operations had dropped more than three million litres of water across the affected provinces, including over one million litres in Riau and more than 780,000 litres in South Kalimantan. He added that weather modification operations was also carried out in West, Central and South Kalimantan and Riau, while the operation was not carried out in Jambi and South Sumatra due to no potential of rain clouds in the atmosphere. The operations helped optimise rainfall in parts of South Kalimantan and Riau, with rain also recorded in West Kalimantan, he told an online press conference on Tuesday. Separately, Indonesian National Armed Forces information centre chief Maj Gen Muhammad Nasir said the military had placed 80,026 personnel on standby or deployed nationwide to tackle forest and land fires, including 1,260 additional troops sent from outside affected areas to reinforce operations, particularly in West Kalimantan. He said another 1,482 personnel had been deployed for a month-long prevention campaign to educate communities about the dangers and wider impact of forest and land burning, including fires caused deliberately or through negligence. Kerajaan tidak lagi luluskan loji janakuasa arang batu

Kuala Lumpur: Kerajaan tidak lagi meluluskan mana-mana loji janakuasa berasaskan arang batu dengan fasa penamatan dijangka berakhir sekitar 2044. Menteri Ekonomi, Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir berkata, pada masa sama Malaysia menjangkakan keperluan kira-kira 9 gigawatt (GW) untuk dimasukkan ke dalam sistem melalui loji janakuasa gas. Beliau berkata, perancangan itu perlu diurus Kementerian Peralihan Tenaga dan Transformasi Air (PETRA) serta Suruhanjaya Tenaga bagi memastikan permintaan dapat diurus dan pada masa sama kekal komited terhadap usaha mengurangkan jejak karbon dalam sektor tenaga. "Dari segi komitmen kerajaan, kita sememangnya tidak lagi meluluskan mana-mana loji janakuasa berasaskan arang batu dan fasa penamatan itu akan berakhir sekitar tahun 2044. Itu akan menjadi loji janakuasa arang batu terakhir yang ditamatkan operasinya. "Pada masa sama, berdasarkan angka yang dikongsikan, kita menjangkakan keperluan kira-kira 9 gigawatt untuk dimasukkan ke dalam sistem melalui loji janakuasa gas," katanya selepas merasmikan Energy Regulatory Insights (ERI) dianjurkan Suruhanjaya Tenaga di sini, hari ini. Katanya, cuaca atau iklim yang meningkatkan keperluan sistem penyejukan dan pendingin hawa turut mengubah corak permintaan tenaga. "Melihat ke hadapan, pengurusan permintaan tenaga akan menjadi sama penting dengan pengurusan bekalan tenaga. Jadi, saya fikir untuk tempoh lima hingga 10 tahun akan datang, Malaysia perlu cukup berdisiplin untuk memastikan sistem kita terus dinaik taraf, bukan sahaja dari segi kuasa yang dihasilkan tetapi juga dari segi grid dan infrastruktur supaya sistem kekal mampu milik, selamat dan mampan," katanya. Jelasnya, reformasi tenaga kini bukan lagi sekadar perkara berkaitan sektor atau kawal selia, sebaliknya menjadi teras kepada dasar ekonomi. "Reformasi tenaga bukan lagi hanya perkara sektoral atau kawal selia. Ia adalah teras kepada dasar ekonomi. Kos, kebolehpercayaan dan profil karbon tenaga akan mempengaruhi lokasi pelabur menjalankan operasi, daya saing industri, kepantasan teknologi baharu digunakan serta usaha melindungi kepentingan rakyat," katanya. Dalam pada itu, Akmal berkata keadaan jerebu yang masih berlaku perlu diberi perhatian susulan fenomena El Nino yang dijangka berterusan sehingga pertengahan tahun depan. Katanya, keadaan itu memerlukan perhatian terhadap perkembangan yang bergantung kepada cuaca termasuk aktiviti pertanian dan penternakan. "Namun, kita juga perlu mengambil kira bahawa kesediaan kita untuk mengurangkan kesan keadaan perubahan iklim ini turut berkait dengan isu tenaga. "Corak atau tingkah laku penggunaan tenaga juga boleh memberi kesan. Maksudnya, jika cuaca panas, penggunaan tenaga untuk pendingin hawa juga akan meningkat," katanya. Jelasnya, langkah mitigasi sedang diambil dengan penyelarasan melalui Agensi Pengurusan Bencana Negara (NADMA), termasuk jika terdapat keperluan untuk proses pembenihan awan. Mengenai kesan jangka pendek jerebu terhadap tenaga, beliau berkata, perubahan penggunaan tenaga mungkin berlaku, manakala kesan jangka pendek lebih kepada pihak pengawal selia jika langkah mitigasi perlu diambil.

Pendidikan bumiputera tidak boleh hanya bergantung kuota

KUALA LUMPUR: Kelangsungan pendidikan masyarakat Melayu dan bumiputera pada masa hadapan tidak lagi boleh bergantung kepada kuota semata-mata, sebaliknya perlu ditransformasikan kepada “survival” keupayaan diri. Menteri Pendidikan Tinggi Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir berkata kejayaan golongan itu perlu diukur menerusi kemampuan menguasai bidang kritikal seperti Sains, Teknologi, Kejuruteraan dan Matematik (STEM), penciptaan teknologi baharu serta pemilikan harta intelek. “Ukurannya bukan sekadar berapa ramai yang memasuki universiti, tetapi berapa ramai yang mampu berfikir, menguasai STEM, membina syarikat global dan memimpin institusi bertaraf dunia,” katanya ketika merasmikan Konvensyen Pendidikan Melayu 2026 di sini hari ini. Zambry berkata bagi mencapai matlamat itu, ekosistem pendidikan negara perlu berganjak daripada sekadar menyediakan akses kepada peningkatan kualiti dan kelayakan kepada kompetensi, pekerjaan kepada keusahawanan, serta penggunaan kepada pemilikan teknologi. Beliau berkata bidang Pendidikan dan Latihan Teknikal dan Vokasional (TVET) perlu dijadikan laluan utama pembangunan bakat negara dan bukannya lagi pilihan kedua bagi melahirkan lebih ramai pakar penyelesai masalah dan juruteknik berkemahiran tinggi. Mengulas mengenai naratif kebergantungan golongan bumiputera, Zambry berkata dasar afirmatif masih mempunyai rasional selagi wujud ketidakseimbangan struktur, namun matlamat akhirnya haruslah ke arah pemberdayaan, kecemerlangan dan kemandirian. “Pendidikan Melayu dan Bumiputera tidak boleh selama-lamanya dibina atas naratif…kami perlu dibantu kerana kami lemah. “Naratif masa depan mestilah..kami diberikan peluang untuk menjadi kuat dan setelah kuat, kami mampu berdiri sendiri, memimpin serta membantu orang lain,” katanya. Terdahulu, dalam ucapannya Zambry menekankan kepentingan penguasaan bahasa Melayu sebagai bahasa ilmu dan identiti, manakala bahasa Inggeris serta bahasa lain berfungsi sebagai jambatan untuk bersaing di peringkat global tanpa mengabaikan aspek integriti. “Dalam mengejar kecemerlangan global, kita tidak boleh kehilangan jiwa. Pendidikan mesti melahirkan manusia yang pintar tetapi pada masa yang sama mempunyai akhlak, identiti, integriti dan keberanian moral,” katanya. Mengenai konvensyen berkenaan yang merupakan kesinambungan Kongres Pendidikan Bumiputera pada 1 Mei lepas, Zambry berkata satu resolusi komprehensif akan dirumuskan pada akhir persidangan hari in. Beliau berkata resolusi berkenaan kemudian akan diserahkan kepada Timbalan Perdana Menteri Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi bagi tindakan dasar selanjutnya oleh kerajaan. – BERNAMA
Theta Edge wins Prasarana job to build telecom infrastructure for LRT3

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 8): Theta Edge Bhd (KL: THETA ) has secured a five-year contract from Prasarana Malaysia Bhd to build and operate telecommunications infrastructure along the Light Rail Transit 3 (LRT3) or Shah Alam Line. In a bourse filing on Tuesday, the group said its wholly-owned subsidiary Theta Telecoms Sdn Bhd (TTEL) has been appointed by Prasarana’s unit Prasarana Integrated Development Sdn Bhd as the network operator and strategic partner for the development of a common telecommunications network infrastructure along the LRT3 right of way. Under the contract, Theta Telecoms will install, operate, maintain and service the required telecommunications hardware and provide network telecommunications services along the LRT3 corridor. Prasarana will receive the higher of RM500,000-a-year or 13% of the project’s gross revenue, with the remaining revenue accruing to Theta Telecoms. The initial contract runs for five years from Sept 1 and may be renewed for two successive five-year periods, subject to Prasarana’s assessment of Theta Telecoms’ performance and compliance with the contract terms, said Theta Edge. The group said that as strategic partner, Theta Telecoms will monetise LRT3’s right of way through telecommunications services along the tracks, stations and other developments, as well as value-added services targeting enterprise customers. Theta Telecoms will also be responsible for the design, installation, protection and maintenance of all cables, fibre, trunking, equipment and other infrastructure within the railway right of way, ensuring these do not interfere with train operations or existing railway, signalling, power, communications and safety systems. “The project represents an opportunity for Theta to leverage on its existing expertise and venture into a recurring income generating project to ensure a steady stream of revenue and cashflow in the future and ride on the future data demand growth in the area,” Theta Edge said. It said the project will be funded through internally generated funds or borrowings. As at end-June, the group had cash of RM23.85 million and total borrowings of RM9.14 million. Theta Edge has been loss-making annually since 2024. For the six months ended June 30, 2026, its net loss narrowed to RM7.77 million from RM10.21 million a year earlier, while revenue increased to RM11.58 million from RM9.03 million. Stealth Solutions Sdn Bhd is Theta Edge’s largest shareholder, with a 27.28% stake following Lembaga Tabung Haji’s disposal of its entire stake on Jan 6. Stealth Solutions is 75%-owned by Datuk Amrul Hisyam Alias and 25% by Norul Azwani Mohd Hanafi, according to the Companies Commission of Malaysia. Shares of Theta Edge closed down half a sen or 0.78% to 63.5 sen on Tuesday, giving the ICT solutions provider a market capitalisation of RM74.32 million.

Do not wait for it to happen,” he said, adding that the government should also explore the use of large drones capable of carrying and dropping water in frontline firefighting operations. National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) chief Suharyanto said 72,009 hectares had been burned across the six priority provinces – West Kalimantan, Riau, South Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan, South Sumatra and Jambi – with 71,069.65 hectares extinguished and another 939.45 hectares still being tackled as of Monday. He said West Kalimantan recorded the largest cumulative burned area at about 38,000 hectares, followed by Riau, which had the largest area still under firefighting operations on Monday. About 97 hectares remained under firefighting operations in West Kalimantan. Outside the six priority provinces, Suharyanto said another 705.1 hectares were affected, including 458 hectares at Bukit Soeharto in the IKN area of East Kalimantan and 223.5 hectares in Teluk Bintuni, West Papua, with smaller fires reported in East and Central Java. He said 55 aircraft were supporting firefighting operations, comprising 36 for water bombing and 19 for weather modification and patrols, while three additional Chinook helicopters from Japan were expected on Wednesday and would initially be deployed in West Kalimantan. Meanwhile, National Police Chief Gen Listyo Sigit Prabowo said police were handling 200 reports related to forest and land fires, with 138 suspects identified, including 119 cases involving deliberate burning, while eight corporations were also being investigated. He said police were conducting further investigations into another 18 companies, while 42 companies had been subjected to administrative sanctions, including the suspension or revocation of permits. Responding to the enforcement update, Prabowo ordered further investigations into companies linked to land that was rapidly converted into plantations after fires, saying he wanted the names and ownership of the corporations involved identified. “If necessary, we should immediately revoke all their permits, their land-use rights and so on. Menteri Pelaburan, Perdagangan dan Industri (MITI), Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani berkata, kehidupan pekerja tempatan berbeza berbanding pekerja asing kerana mereka mempunyai pendidikan dan kelayakan tertentu. Menurut beliau, perkara itu perlu diambil kira oleh industri ketika menentukan struktur gaji supaya pekerjaan ditawarkan mempunyai nilai ekonomi yang menarik kepada rakyat tempatan. “Ada orang beritahu saya, mereka dah tawar (pekerjaan), tapi rakyat tempatan tak mahu terima. Jefferies fund accuses Radiant World of fraud over fake invoices

(Sept 8): A fund managed by Jefferies Financial Group Inc has accused Radiant World of falsifying iron ore invoices as part of a “fraudulent scheme” against it in a US$500 million (RM2 billion) London court claim. The lawsuit was filed in late August and led a judge to impose a worldwide freezing order against Radiant World and its founder, as Bloomberg previously reported. However, the details of the claim have not previously been made public, and the case represents one of the first public accusations of fraud against Radiant World from one of its major lenders. In a summary of its claim filed at the High Court and made public on Tuesday, LAM Trade Finance Group II LLC accused the defendants in the case of perpetrating a “fraudulent scheme” that induced the fund to pay “large sums” to both Radiant World Corporation Pte, the company’s main operating unit, and Sapphire Minmetals Corporation Ltd, a closely related but legally separate company. “This included falsification of invoices, notices of assignment, contracts, and email correspondence,” the fund, which is run by Point Bonita, part of the US firm’s asset management division, said in the claim form. “The claimant’s investigations revealed that the fraud had been concealed from it for some time.” The defendants are Radiant World’s main Singapore operating company, its Hong Kong holding company, its founder and majority shareholder Pinkesh Nahar, Sapphire Minmetals and its majority owner Rakesh Sethi. Spokespeople for Jefferies and Radiant World did not immediately respond to emails seeking comment. Sethi, Sapphire’s chairman and majority owner, had no immediate comment when reached by phone on Tuesday. Bloomberg reported in July that several top commodity traders had stopped doing business with Radiant World amid concerns it had provided falsified documents to banks to raise financing. Radiant World denied wrongdoing and said it conducts its business to the highest commercial and legal standards. The Jefferies claim is for more than US$500 million, according to its legal filing, without clarifying how this was calculated. Bloomberg previously reported that the fund’s exposure to Radiant World was less than US$300 million and its exposure to Sapphire Minmetals was much smaller than that. The Jefferies fund is also seeking a freezing injunction against Radiant World, Sapphire Minmetals and their majority owners in Singapore, with a hearing due to be heard on Wednesday. MACC to charge former Tabung Haji chairman Abdul Azeez on Wednesday

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 8): The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is set to charge former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim on Wednesday over the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the institution. According to the MACC, Abdul Azeez’s case will be heard before Sessions Court judge Azura Alwi at 9am. He will be the most high-profile person charged over the RCI findings. On Sept 3, two former managers of TH Properties, Nasahruddin Ahmad, 56, and Tengku Kamaruddin, 55, claimed trial at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court to charges of criminal breach of trust and abetment for allegedly pocketing RM72,000 in penalties imposed on contractors. Sessions Court judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud subsequently fixed Sept 24 for Adi Azuan to appear in court to face the charges. Abdul Azeez was among former senior Tabung Haji management and board members, including a former chief executive officer, a former Treasury secretary general and former Islamic affairs minister Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom, who were remanded by the MACC over allegations arising from the RCI. The RCI report, made public on July 29, documented various management and operational weaknesses involving Tabung Haji between 2014 and 2020, and identified several problematic investments requiring a forensic audit. The report also highlighted evidence of suspicious transactions and the concealment of information. Abdul Azeez, a former Baling member of Parliament, was acquitted of nine charges in 2022 — three for corruption and six for money laundering. The acquittal was granted after the prosecution did not object to his application. His lawyer said the MACC had completed its investigation and decided to take no further action against him, with all seized assets and property returned. ASEAN Needs To Review Mechanisms To Handle Transboundary Haze - Anwar

PUTRAJAYA, Sept 8 (Bernama) -- ASEAN needs to review the existing mechanisms in dealing with the issue of transboundary haze to avoid adverse impacts on the people's health, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said ASEAN ministers need to pay serious attention to the matter as the haze can have a direct impact on the health and lives of the people, especially children and babies. “There is room for improvement. I think the ASEAN ministers must seriously look at it, because this is affecting lives, particularly of children, and babies, and if we have seen in Serian (it) is really concerning,” he said. Anwar, who is also the Minister of Finance, said this to the media after attending a Meeting with the staff of the Ministry of Plantations and Commodities here today. Air quality in Serian was reported to have returned to hazardous levels when the monitoring station at the district police headquarters (IPD) in the area recorded an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 302 this morning. Last Friday, His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia declared a haze emergency in the entire Serian division following air pollution that was hazardous to public health, before the declaration was lifted yesterday. The Prime Minister stressed that the issue of open burning in Indonesia needs to be thoroughly investigated, including identifying the real cause of the fire before any action or accusations are made against any party. Asked if there are Malaysian companies operating in the republic that have committed wrongdoings that have contributed to the haze issue, Anwar said the country respects any legal action by the Indonesian authorities. "If there are Malaysian companies that are affected (involved), we will give Indonesia space to take action. We will certainly respect the actions there and we will not defend (them)," he said. He stressed that Malaysia will not intervene or protect any company if investigations prove they are responsible for open burning or other violations of the law in neighbouring countries. The ASEAN Parliamentarians for Human Rights (APHR) had warned that the region's transboundary haze crisis has become a human rights emergency, one that ASEAN and its member states must address with urgency. It urges ASEAN and its member states to treat the worsening transboundary haze problem as a human rights emergency, and to use the upcoming Conference of the Parties to the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution in Da Nang, Vietnam, this October to close the enforcement gap that has left the region breathing toxic air for nearly three decades. Among others, APHR also urged ASEAN and member states to develop a regional legal framework to hold corporate entities accountable for forest fires due to peatland drainage, and commodity-driven deforestation and agricultural residue burning. It also urged mandating all plantation companies with concession areas in flammable landscapes including peatland or forestland to publicly disclose and publish concession maps to be shared across all ASEAN member states to improve transparency in their supply chains. Other than that, APHR urged the ASEAN member countries to regulate traceability requirements at every step of the supply chain of agribusiness and food industry to identify the origin of commodities and mitigate risks of deforestation, crop residue burning and transboundary haze at the source. Pendidikan bumiputera perlu beralih daripada kuota kepada keupayaan diri

KUALA LUMPUR – Kelangsungan pendidikan masyarakat Melayu dan bumiputera pada masa hadapan tidak lagi boleh bergantung kepada kuota semata-mata, sebaliknya perlu ditransformasikan kepada “survival” keupayaan diri. Menteri Pendidikan Tinggi Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir berkata, kejayaan golongan itu perlu diukur menerusi kemampuan menguasai bidang kritikal seperti Sains, Teknologi, Kejuruteraan dan Matematik (STEM), penciptaan teknologi baharu serta pemilikan harta intelek. “Ukurannya bukan sekadar berapa ramai yang memasuki universiti, tetapi berapa ramai yang mampu berfikir, menguasai STEM, membina syarikat global dan memimpin institusi bertaraf dunia,” katanya ketika merasmikan Konvensyen Pendidikan Melayu 2026 di sini hari ini. Zambry berkata bagi mencapai matlamat itu, ekosistem pendidikan negara perlu berganjak daripada sekadar menyediakan akses kepada peningkatan kualiti dan kelayakan kepada kompetensi, pekerjaan kepada keusahawanan, serta penggunaan kepada pemilikan teknologi. Terdahulu, dalam ucapannya Zambry menekankan kepentingan penguasaan bahasa Melayu sebagai bahasa ilmu dan identiti, manakala bahasa Inggeris serta bahasa lain berfungsi sebagai jambatan untuk bersaing di peringkat global tanpa mengabaikan aspek integriti. “Dalam mengejar kecemerlangan global, kita tidak boleh kehilangan jiwa. Tata mine feud divides locals as Ruto pushes firm to leave Kenya

(Sept 8): Kenyan President William Ruto withdrew a century-old concession for Indian behemoth Tata Group to mine soda ash in an area inhabited by Maasai herders near Tanzania, arguing the conglomerate hasn’t built any processing facilities that benefit the nation. Residents of the villages around Lake Magadi, Africa’s biggest for the trona mineral that’s converted into soda ash, are split on whether Tata should stay on or leave. The company’s chemicals unit bankrolls four schools in the poverty-stricken county of Kajiado, staffs a hospital and supplies fresh water used in Magadi town. Its private railway replenishes cattle-watering points along a 145km line for free and it also operates a train service charging people from the community a mere US$0.30 (RM1.21) for long distances. For Ruto, this isn’t enough: he told the Mumbai-based firm “to pack and go” because it has been exporting soda ash made from minerals extracted from the lake instead of processing it locally to make glass, cleaning products and batteries for electric vehicles. The president’s tiff with Tata — whose 32 companies generated combined revenue of about US$185 billion in the year through March and make everything from salt to steel and cars — highlights the tensions between communities, governments and investors over exploiting natural wealth while avoiding a phenomenon economists call “the resource curse", or the failure to translate that bounty into better living standards. By shipping the soda ash to India — the world’s fastest-growing major economy and where Tata provides the mineral for one in every five beverage bottles — Kenya is missing out on the economic benefits of that trade, government officials argue. That amounts to “exporting potential factories, potential jobs, technology and opportunities for our engineers, chemists, technicians, transporters, entrepreneurs and young people,” Principal Secretary for Industrialisation Juma Mukhwana said. “No strategic raw material should leave Africa without first asking whether we can competitively transform it here.” Tata Chemicals Magadi Ltd has responded to the matters raised by the Kenyan government, including providing information on its compliance with regulatory requirements, and is awaiting the mines ministry’s review and further direction, it said in response to questions. Even in India and the US, where Tata Chemicals Ltd has soda-ash manufacturing plants, it does not have downstream manufacturing facilities such as glass, it said. Tata should be given an opportunity to continue operations, said Rose Saroni, a community mobiliser in Magadi. “Let’s sit down and talk about the community grievances and how they can be addressed,” she said, adding that access to clean water will be compromised if Tata leaves. Other leaders support the president’s move. “We are entitled by law to get benefits” such as a share of royalties, said Isaac Keses Kiresian, a local-government lawmaker representing the ward where Tata’s mines are located. “Unfortunately, it has been push and pull with the company.” The opposition Democracy for the Citizens Party sees the move as a decoy to push Tata out of a region with “huge deposits” of lithium and oil, it said in a statement. Lake Magadi falls within Block 14T, an onshore oil-exploration area belonging to state-owned National Oil Corp. But the shallow, pink-tinted lake isn’t a money spinner. Last year, Tata’s operation exported about US$57 million of soda ash. It’s the sole domestic producer of the chemical used by water utilities including the firm that serves Nairobi, the capital, to regulate the acidity and alkalinity of drinking water. Kenya is the fourth-ranked producer of natural soda ash, accounting for 1% of global production. Tata is also embroiled in a dispute with Kajiado county’s government, which is demanding 12.2 billion shillings (RM381.15 million) in historical unpaid land rates. Industri perlu percepat penggunaan automasi elak kebergantungan pekerja asing

Kuala Lumpur: Industri perlu mempercepatkan penggunaan automasi dalam operasi dan pengeluaran bagi mengurangkan kebergantungan terhadap pekerja asing, khususnya apabila bekalan tenaga kerja itu tidak lagi dapat dipertahankan pada kadar seperti sekarang. Menteri Pelaburan, Perdagangan dan Industri (MITI), Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani berkata, pendekatan itu perlu dilaksanakan merentasi semua saiz syarikat, termasuk perusahaan mikro, kecil dan sederhana (PMKS), bagi memastikan industri bersedia menghadapi perubahan dalam pasaran tenaga kerja. "Dari soal industri, kita nak banyak syarikat tak kira apa saiz, sama ada mikro, kecil, sederhana. Kita nak bagi penerangan betapa pentingnya bahawa kita kena bawa automasi ke dalam operasi dan juga pengeluaran kita ini dengan secepat mungkin," katanya kepada media selepas menyampaikan ucapan perasmian penutup Voices of HER Forum 2026 di sini, hari ini. Johari berkata, bekalan pekerja asing pada masa depan tidak boleh lagi diharapkan pada kadar seperti sekarang, sekali gus menjadikan automasi antara pendekatan yang perlu diberi perhatian oleh industri. Katanya, pekerja asing pula sepatutnya digunakan bagi pekerjaan yang tergolong dalam kategori 3D iaitu sukar, berbahaya dan kotor, manakala pekerjaan lain perlu dinilai dari segi keperluan serta nilai ekonomi kepada pekerja tempatan. "Pada masa akan datang, kita tidak boleh lagi memiliki pekerja asing pada kadar seperti yang ada sekarang" katanya. Beliau berkata, kelonggaran pengambilan pekerja asing sebelum ini membolehkan jumlahnya mencecah 2.6 juta, dengan kumpulan itu membantu melaksanakan pekerjaan 3D supaya pengeluaran dapat dilakukan dan seterusnya meningkatkan eksport. Bagaimanapun, beliau menegaskan, penggunaan pekerja asing bukan bertujuan menggantikan pekerja tempatan kerana struktur kehidupan pekerja tempatan berbeza, termasuk mempunyai keluarga, pendidikan dan kelulusan. Katanya, jika industri terus diberikan kelonggaran dalam penggunaan pekerja asing, ia boleh menimbulkan masalah dari sudut persaingan antara syarikat yang mempunyai akses kepada pekerja asing dengan syarikat yang tidak mempunyai akses sama. "Kalau kita bagi fleksibiliti sampai 2.6 juta pekerja asing, jadi mereka ini sebenarnya kita bawa dalam negara untuk membantu melaksanakan kerja-kerja 3D," katanya. Sehubungan itu, Johari berkata, kerajaan mahu mempromosikan ekonomi digital, platform digital dan automasi supaya pada satu tahap industri tidak lagi bergantung kepada pekerja asing kecuali bagi pekerjaan 3D. Beliau berkata, pendekatan itu juga penting untuk mewujudkan padang persaingan sama rata dalam kalangan syarikat, khususnya apabila struktur kos buruh menjadi antara faktor yang mempengaruhi keupayaan sesebuah syarikat untuk berkembang. "Bila kita tidak lagi bergantung kepada pekerja asing, semua syarikat berada pada kedudukan yang sama. Jadi, kalau gaji pekerja meningkat, semua syarikat perlu menaikkan gaji pada kadar sama," katanya. Pada masa sama, Johari berkata, isu gaji turut memainkan peranan penting dalam keputusan pekerja tempatan menerima sesuatu pekerjaan kerana mereka akan melihat nilai ekonomi yang diperoleh daripada pekerjaan berkenaan. Beliau memberi contoh rakyat Malaysia yang sanggup berulang-alik ke Singapura untuk bekerja walaupun perjalanan mengambil masa lebih satu jam kerana melihat nilai ekonomi yang diperoleh daripada pekerjaan itu. Katanya, apabila pekerjaan tidak memberikan nilai ekonomi yang dirasakan mencukupi, pekerja tempatan mungkin memilih pekerjaan lain yang menawarkan pulangan harian dan fleksibiliti lebih baik. "Bila pekerjaan itu tidak mempunyai nilai ekonomi yang menarik, akhirnya mereka memilih untuk buat kerja seperti bawa e-hailing daripada bekerja dalam sektor berkenaan," katanya. Dalam pada itu, Johari berkata, mana-mana industri yang tampil kepada MITI untuk mendapatkan pekerja asing perlu terlebih dahulu menjelaskan pekerjaan 3D yang hendak diisi, selain menyatakan gaji permulaan dan kelayakan bagi pekerjaan yang bukan dalam kategori berkenaan. Beliau berkata, pengurangan pekerja asing bukan 3D tidak akan dilakukan secara serta-merta, sebaliknya perlu dilaksanakan secara berperingkat mengikut keperluan industri. "Kalau sebelum ini syarikat mempunyai 1,000 pekerja dan 20 peratus daripadanya dalam pekerjaan 3D, bermakna 200 pekerja adalah untuk kerja 3D, manakala 800 lagi perlu dikurangkan secara berperingkat. Ia bukan dilakukan serta-merta, tetapi perlu dikurangkan dari semasa ke semasa," katanya.
